detail.abstract: This paper investigates the structural and identity transformation of L'Oréal Paris within the French mass-retail market (1997-2026). Challenging conventional narratives of seamless digital transition, we deploy a critical hermeneutic framework combining Ricoeur's philosophy (Mêmeté vs. Ipséité), Weickian sensemaking, Schmittian political theology (Katechon), and critical Resource Dependence Theory (RDT). We demonstrate that the mid-2010s eviction of key competitors through predatory proliferation did not signal a return to consumer intimacy, but rather the brand's entry into "cold identity." Facing narrative exhaustion, the organization deployed AI diagnostics and Beauty Tech as an algorithmic Katechon-a technological shield designed to freeze market decline and substitute scientific hyper-personalization for lost mythological resonance. This shift marks the absolute triumph of Sameness over Selfhood, transforming the brand from an emancipatory storyteller into an automated platform for appearance optimization. Methodologically grounded in critical organizational analysis, this study exposes the systemic blind spots of managerial literature by revealing how technological interfaces enforce cognitive hegemony and transition consumers from relational Customer Lock-on to existential Customer Lock-in.

detail.abstract: People in similar socioeconomic circumstances often display strikingly different financial behaviours. We examined whether these individual differences are well-explained by broad personality traits, domain-specific money attitudes, and financial literacy. Using data from a UK sample (N = 1,366), we jointly modelled multiple financial behaviours, including consumption, saving, cash holdings, and financial monitoring. Money attitudes emerged as the strongest and most consistent psychological predictors, exhibiting larger associations than personality traits and financial literacy. Some traits showed comparatively small, behaviour-specific effects, whereas financial literacy primarily predicted portfolio allocation and disposable income. Overall, the findings suggest that consequential financial behaviours are shaped by layered psychological influences, with domain-specific attitudes explaining substantially more behavioural heterogeneity than broad personality traits or financial knowledge.

detail.abstract: AI video platforms must decide whether generation should earn its own margin or be supported by advertising from finished content. Improving a video often requires additional paid attempts, making token pricing a determinant of both output and quality. We study an integrated platform that chooses token pricing, creator advertising compensation, and computing capacity, while creators choose participation, completed output, and quality. A technological threshold governs the optimal contract: whether tokens per completed project rise more or less than proportionally with quality. At feasible interior optima below this threshold, the token price exceeds marginal computing cost and the creator share at least equals advertising elasticity. Above the threshold, both comparisons reverse. With the modeled operating and capacity costs, the platform can optimally run generation at a loss while retaining sufficient advertising revenue to cover it. Yet its contract supports fewer creators and projects than the allocation maximizing combined platform and creator monetary surplus. Cheaper generation therefore need not imply stronger participation incentives. For quadratic token requirements, we characterize the global optimum, including free generation and full advertising sharing. An analytical extension establishes that the technological threshold survives competition for creators at regular interior equilibria, while generation profitability also depends on residual creator supply. These results show how the computational demands of quality determine the division of earnings between creation tools and content monetization, and why managers must evaluate token charges and creator compensation together.

detail.abstract: An online marketplace decides how consumers, firms, and the platform share the cost of product returns. We study this decision when the platform earns commissions and sells prominent placement. Consumers inspect, try, and return products; firms bid for the first position and then set prices. Earlier display attracts more trials but can retain a smaller fraction of them. For small positive losses, assigning return costs to consumers raises the value of prominence relative to reimbursing firms by the same amount. Advertising therefore shifts the platform's preferred division of a given return bill toward consumers. We characterize the joint allocation for small positive return losses and give a cost condition under which the platform pays nothing. In markets with frequent returns, the platform can instead share the bill with consumers: a higher commission makes it pay more to encourage shopping and retained sales. Results at finite losses show that advertising can change the optimal policy from firm-paid free returns to full consumer payment, reducing both commissions and consumer surplus. This advertising-induced policy change can lower or raise total welfare, depending on whether savings from fewer trials and returns offset the loss from reduced participation.

detail.abstract: Behavioral instruments administered by enumerators are increasingly used to measure latent traits, on the premise that they remove the respondent's subjectivity. Both self reported and behavioral formats require an evaluator, the respondent or the enumerator, and therefore reallocate rather than eliminate subjectivity. Taking socio-emotional skills as a case, where both formats are routinely used, we draw on baseline data from a randomized controlled trial in Tanzania (4,620 youth, 46 enumerators) that examines 14 skills measured in both formats. We show that enumerators account for 31% of the variance in behavioral scores against 7% in self-reports. The gap holds for every skill, and is not explained by observable characteristics, limiting the ability to adjust ex post. The cross-format discordance is not driven by enumerators: the formats disagree just as much within enumerators, suggesting that they capture different skill dimensions. It is therefore essential to assign enumerators independently of the groups being compared and conduct involved enumerator training to standardize the administration and scoring of measures.

detail.abstract: We study whether patent grants facilitate personal and professional recognition, leading to the reallocation of inventive talent across startups and incumbent firms. Using examiner leniency as exogenous variation in first patent grants, we find that becoming an inventor increases entry into high-growth entrepreneurship: successful first-time applicants are more likely to found VC-backed startups and to join VC-backed startups as employees. Receipt of a first patent also increases retention, promotion, and transitions to higher-prestige employers. While their employers generally retain the property rights, inventors gain recognition and benefit from expanded professional networks, collaborations with superstar inventors, and greater leadership skills. Becoming an inventor is also linked to technological specialization and higher-quality subsequent innovation. Through these channels, named inventorship produces externalities that extend far beyond property rights, reshaping outside options and talent allocation.

detail.abstract: Emerging market consumers are different from developed world consumers, and existing information search models may be inadequate to characterize their search strategies. We develop a model of consumer information search positing that offline social capital enables relatively uneducated and rural consumers to search by relying heavily on networks in their community. Using a sample of 807 consumers, our Tobit estimates demonstrate that high offline social capital is positively associated with information search involving talking to friends, relatives, and community members, and negatively related to viewing advertisements or discussion with salespeople. We find that internet-using consumers with high online social capital use more e-Word-of-Mouth search. Our results indicate that firms attempting to penetrate rural markets in emerging economies should use strategies that leverage offline social capital.

detail.abstract: Technical measures of general-purpose AI capabilities are increasingly used to anticipate AI's societal impacts, particularly on the labor market. This capability-centered account has growing influence in AI policy and governance, yet offers limited explanatory power for the actual outcomes of organizational AI deployment and effects on workers. We argue that organizational projects causally mediate the effect of AI capabilities on societal outcomes, and play a key role in determining which human-AI labor relations obtain and whether pro-worker outcomes emerge. Drawing on a theory-generating case of AI-assisted academic advising at a large US public university, we identify three empirical puzzles for capability-centered accounts of AI's impacts: divergent outcomes from similar predictive AI capabilities, workforce expansion following AI adoption, and the decoupling of capabilities from organizational arrangements. Building on organization theory, we develop an analytical account of an organizational project of AI that comprises five constitutive elementsproblems, theories of change, actions, human-AI labor relations, and metrics-and examine where organizational mediation of AI capabilities occurs. We identify the phenomenon of flexible substitution (overlapping human and AI capabilities that admits a range of organizationally plausible divisions of labor) as a key source of organizational flexibility. Contrasting case studies from K-12 education, healthcare, and frontier AI development illustrate how different organizational objectives and institutional environments promote or constrain the possibility of pro-worker outcomes. Our framework suggests that realizing pro-worker outcomes requires institutional conditions that make pro-worker organizational projects of AI desirable and sustainable. The organizational-project account of AI's societal impact offers an actionable alternative to the determinism of the capability-centered account, helping researchers, policymakers, leaders, and organizers alike attend to the normative implications of choices around AI's deployment in organizations.

detail.abstract: This viewpoint article argues that Information Systems (IS) professionals must evolve their design practices to effectively harness insights from user-generated content (UGC). While participatory and user-centered design remain foundational, they struggle to scale and anticipate emerging needs in today's dynamic digital ecosystems. We introduce the Lead UX framework, which integrates von Hippel's lead user theory with data-analytic approaches to systematically identify both innovation-driving lead users and key emergent lead topics within large-scale user discussions. By combining automated topic modeling and related natural language processing techniques with expert human review, Lead UX enables IS professionals to transform overwhelming volumes of UGC into actionable intelligence for proactive, innovation-driven design. We outline a hybrid workflow for operationalizing Lead UX, address challenges such as data quality and analytic bias, and propose future research directions, including comparative case studies, practitioner assessments, and algorithmic benchmarking. Finally, we offer actionable recommendations for educators and practitioners on embedding Lead UX into curricula and development processes, positioning users as co-designers in continuous IS innovation.

detail.abstract: R&D intensity, per capita GDP, and per capita CO2 emissions links in the USA over the period of 1870-2020 reflects the evolution of the economic development and technology for the environment benefit. Using Time varying Granger causality, the empirical results indicate both causal links between R&D intensity and per capita CO2 emissions and between per capita GDP and per capita CO2 emissions are time varying. In addition, R&D intensity significantly affects per capita CO2 emissions since 1975, and the per capita GDP significantly influences per capita CO2 emissions since 1978. That is, these findings not only in supportive of the EKC theory, but further disentangle the subtly linkages for the R&D intensity and CO2 emissions and the per capita GDP and CO2 emissions. Finally, the policy implication is that launch the new technical innovation and increase in R&D investment to maintain its sustainable economic growth are the best government strategy to reduce CO2 emissions in the USA.

detail.abstract: Cybersecurity incidents affecting operational technology (OT) in municipal drinking-water systems can propagate from digital compromise to process disruption, recovery expenditure, and fiscal stress, yet these consequences are rarely quantified within public-sector financial planning. This study develops an empirical-probabilistic framework integrating infrastructure exposure, verified governmental ownership, observed cybersecurity evidence, water-specific financial capacity, rare-event loss modeling, and uncertainty-aware cybersecurity investment. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Seventh Drinking Water Infrastructure Needs Survey and Assessment (DWINSA) records were aggregated into 3,518 drinking-water systems representing $313.405 billion in observed unadjusted infrastructure need. Need is strongly concentrated (Gini = 0.786, 95% bootstrap CI: 0.759-0.812), with the largest 10% of systems accounting for 67.34% of observed need. Median per-capita need decreases from $4,395 for small systems to $1,526 and $928 for medium and large systems, respectively (H = 1092.43, p = 6.05 × 10-238). Linkage with EPA Safe Drinking Water Information System records identifies 2,447 active local-government systems, and conservative linkage to U.S. Census government-finance records yields 752 systems with usable water-specific revenue and expenditure. Repeated five-fold cross-validation shows that Extra Trees explains approximately 90.8% of variation in log infrastructure need, with population, pipe length, and service connections dominating held-out permutation importance. Independent federal and state cybersecurity evidence is used to anchor a conditional lognormal loss envelope. Under a 5% disruptive-event incidence scenario, median annual expected loss is $14,397 and median CVaR 0.95 is $287,935; the corresponding median tail burden equals 2.19% of annual water revenue and 2.45% of annual water expenditure. Variance-based sensitivity analysis attributes most output uncertainty to incidence and severity assumptions, and heavier-tailed severity models raise the share of systems whose tail loss is at least 5% of water expenditure from 20.9% to between 22.3% and 60.8%. An evidence-referenced experiment over all 128 portfolios of seven control families shows that, at budgets of 1-2% of water expenditure, expected-loss minimization favors frequency-reducing controls whereas robust tailrisk minimization favors consequence-reducing controls; the two objectives converge at larger budgets. The framework provides a reproducible approach for translating heterogeneous infrastructure, cyber-event, and fiscal evidence into explicitly conditional cyber-financial risk measures.

detail.abstract: A global Microsoft 365 outage on 12 and 13 November 2026 revived the question of whether NHS organisations should bring systems back on-premises. This paper argues that the better question is what minimum of care must remain possible, for which patients and for how long, when shared digital dependencies fail, and who must demonstrate it. Drawing on the public record of the outage, the 2026 military strikes on cloud data centres, National Cyber Security Centre reporting on state-linked cyber activity, the 10 Year Health Plan, national emergency preparedness arrangements, and current clinical safety, medical device, cyber and data law, it proposes Isolation Tiers: a classification of clinical and operational capabilities by minimum clinical service, isolation endurance, recovery tolerance, safe capacity and recovery integrity. It builds on controls NHS cyber assurance already requires and proposes a way to specify and test the minimum service each capability must sustain. The resulting architecture is cloud-centred with a deliberately engineered local layer. It is assessed at site, provider and population-service level, governed through a dependency register that separates demonstrated controls, by test level, from planned controls and unmitigated dependencies, and tested through graded exercises at each level. The paper separates what an NHS trust can decide from what rests with suppliers and national bodies, and asks the Department of Health and Social Care for common digital-disruption planning assumptions and for demonstrated survivability of national platforms that support essential care. The architecture is offered for critical examination and has not been empirically validated.

Background. A person cared for at home depends on one agency; when it closes, visits stop. An earlier study by the author found that a rule reserving for people the tasks that must stay human (the task-reservation rule) protects the value of care better than five alternatives and raises agencies' costs. Payment returns only part of that cost. Who pays the rest?

Methods. A simulation calibrated on 6,689 US home health agencies. Each agency was placed under six settings, including no rule, in 1,024 runs. The closure test, not fitted to observed closures, was moved from lenient to strict. Hypotheses and verdict rules were registered publicly before any sweep was run (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/HKTJP).

Results. At the registered closure test the task-reservation rule closed 304 [205, 439] agencies (median [2.5, 97.5]) that stayed open with no rule and kept none open that would have closed: a net loss of 2.04 [1.43, 3.00] percentage points of capacity (F2, supported). The direction was the same at every closure test examined. In no run was the setting first on value also first on retained capacity (F6, not supported). The rule closed 6.2 of every 100 agencies in the smallest quarter and 2.5 in the largest (F4, supported); counted in patients, the largest quarter carried 37.5% of the loss. Agencies with the largest share of patients who qualify for both Medicare and Medicaid were closed less often in 93.4% of runs (F3, indeterminate). Mean quality among remaining agencies rose in every run, largely because lower-quality agencies had closed.

Conclusions. In this model, when payment does not cover the cost of the rule, the cost is paid in the closure of the agencies with the weakest finances. A payment covering that cost was not tested, and the counts are levels at a stated closure test, not forecasts.

detail.abstract: Gig delivery workers play a critical role in fulfilling online food orders but often lack reliable access to basic workplace amenities, including restrooms. Because delivery platforms provide no physical facilities, workers frequently depend on restaurants for restroom access during order pickups. This study examines how improving restroom access for delivery workers affects delivery operations and restaurant activity. We exploit a policy implemented in New York City (NYC) that requires restaurants partnered with food delivery platforms to grant delivery workers restroom access during pickups. Using a difference-indifferences design that compares platform-partnered restaurants in NYC with comparable restaurants in Chicago, we estimate a 4.8% increase in weekly restaurant visits, including a 6.1% increase in takeout visits and a 2.4% increase in dine-in visits. The effects vary across restaurants: chain restaurants experience larger overall gains, while independent restaurants with limited staffing capacity benefit less, particularly in dine-in activity. Additional analyses reveal increased takeout-related visits in areas with limited public restroom availability and improved delivery-speed ratings, consistent with reduced operational frictions for delivery workers. Together, these findings suggest that improving access to basic amenities for delivery workers can generate operational and market benefits while producing uneven gains across participating firms. More broadly, the study highlights how worker protection policies can help alleviate coordination frictions in platform-mediated markets.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence promises to strengthen how ventures sense opportunities and threats under uncertainty by predicting demand, scanning environments, and evaluating strategic alternatives at negligible cost. Adopting a dynamic capability perspective, we argue that this promise depends on the type of uncertainty a decision involves. AI strengthens sensing and seizing when uncertainty can be resolved through information, but it cannot resolve uncertainty that is revealed only through action. When decision makers fail to distinguish the two, AI produces uncertainty compression, a condition in which perceived uncertainty falls faster than actual uncertainty. Compression leads entrepreneurs to abandon flexibility and commit prematurely to irreversible investments, which weakens the capacity to reconfigure that dynamic capabilities require. We contrast two modes of AI use. In oracle mode, AI resolves uncertainty and selects a single course of action. In generator mode, AI expands, stages, and monitors a portfolio of real options and thereby supports sensing, seizing, and transforming. We develop propositions specifying when each mode improves decisions and how entrepreneurial theorizing and the competitive diffusion of AI condition these effects. The framework reframes AI not as a substitute for entrepreneurial judgment but as a technology that changes the economics of flexibility and, when used as a generator, serves as a microfoundation of dynamic capabilities.

detail.abstract: Call option prices, viewed as functions of strike and time-to-expiration, are totally positive of order 2 (TP2) if the ratio of the price of a higher-strike call to a lower-strike call increases with time-to-expiration. A corresponding property applies to put option prices. Prior work has developed conditions for these properties to hold for European options; here we establish these properties for American options. The key condition we require is that log returns on the underlying asset have a log-concave density. Gaussian densities provide an important special case. Within our framework, we show that total positivity properties hold more broadly for American than European options. Empirically, we find that violations of TP2 properties are infrequent, typically small, and reverse quickly. Trades that bet against violations achieve high hit rates. Violations are more frequent among European than American options, a pattern that is qualitatively consistent with our theoretical results.

detail.abstract:
Small and rural governments finance much of the nation’s water, street, and public safety infrastructure. However, many borrow infrequently, lack in-house debt expertise, and face higher borrowing costs and missed financing opportunities. Published research and regulatory data point to five recurring barriers: limited access to independent, conflict-free advice; thin competition in the sale of small issues; financial reporting gaps; underused subsidized and pooled financing programs; and continuing disclosure lapses that follow a government into future offerings.

This toolkit organizes established practices that address those barriers into a five-stage sequence a small government can follow: assess, prepare, choose, execute, and sustain and measure. It includes the Capital Access Readiness Index (CARI), a 25-item self-assessment that scores readiness across five domains and directs users to priority modules. detail.abstract: We study a two-stage matching process motivated by Re:Match, an EU-funded program that matches Ukrainians to housing in capacitated German cities. In this matching process, first, an initial matching of participants to housing is proposed and matched participants may either accept or withdraw from the program. Then, previously unmatched participants are assigned to the remaining unaccepted capacity and are given the choice to accept or withdraw. We assume that acceptance probabilities are given and prove algorithmic guarantees in two settings-when acceptances are independent and when they are arbitrarily correlated-with respect to a common benchmark: the expected value of the optimal policy under the most favorable distribution of acceptances. In the independent setting, we guarantee a competitive ratio (CR) of 4/5 and prove that a CR exceeding 5/6 is unachievable. In the arbitrarily correlated setting, we guarantee the best possible CR of 3/4. This theoretical analysis is complemented by a description of Re:Match's implementation and matching process.

detail.abstract: Mission-driven organisations are often judged by how quickly they can mobilise people and partners when need spikes. Six propositions address continuity of contact between surges, role progression, repeated partnering, formal and informal processes, reflexive volunteering and the transfer of relationships when staff leave. No original empirical data are presented. The contribution is a bounded argument for treating relationship stewardship as a deliberate, manageable capability.

Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925), this study challenges structuralist fatalism and post-colonial erasures of subaltern voice. It argues that the tragedy of marginalized actors stems not merely from external macro-structural barriers, but from an internal cognitive paralysis split between temporal myopia ("looking too close") and spatial utopianism ("thinking too far"). By redefining fleeting encounters with elite aesthetics as a navigational anchor rather than a deceptive ideological trap (the Polaris Theory), the study illuminates how subaltern reflexivity is awakened through cognitive shame. Subsequently, it maps a non-linear itinerary of incremental capital accumulation (the Plateau Ascent Model) wherein actors surrender the unattainable "sky" to secure an intermediary foothold. Ultimately, establishing sovereignty on this high-ridge empowers subaltern subjects to transition from passive objects of desire to active agents exercising sub-optimal selection, reclaiming secular dignity without relying on grand revolutions.

detail.abstract: State and local governments spend tens of billions of dollars annually on economic development subsidies, but research finds these incentives have minimal impacts on business location and investment, producing little meaningful economic growth. Building on the long and distinguished record on this subject in Economic Development Quarterly, this paper argues subsidies persist despite their weak empirical record due to political economy factors-benefits accruing to stakeholders rather than the broader public-that bear the diffused but high costs. detail.abstract:
This study asks whether cash-flow, valuation, growth and leverage indicators are associated with annual stock returns for six large listed Indian fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies: Hindustan Unilever (HUL), ITC, Britannia Industries, Dabur India, Marico and Godrej Consumer Products (GCPL). The data are consolidated annual-report financials for FY2014-15 to FY2024-25 and split- and bonus-adjusted National Stock Exchange (NSE) closing prices at each 31 March boundary. Returns are price-only.

Before estimation, the dataset was audited cell by cell against the annual reports. The audit found a critical share-base error that had tripled GCPL's FCF yield for FY2015-16 to FY2017-18. It also found audited cash-flow, EPS and revenue figures that had never been carried into the model inputs. Forty-five values were corrected using the annual reports, and every correction is documented.

The primary model was specified before estimation: pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) with year effects and heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors, on 53 firm-years. In it, prior-year earnings-per-share (EPS) growth (b = −0.18, p = 0.26), free-cash-flow (FCF) yield at the start of the year (b = 6.32, p = 0.32) and trailing P/E at the start of the year (b = 0.20, p = 0.65) are not significantly associated with annual returns. Wild-cluster bootstrap p-values are 0.39, 0.40 and 0.72. The FCF-yield coefficient depends on information timing. The FY(t−1) cash flow it uses is published up to 60 days after each window opens. When only information fully public at the start of the window is used (t−2), FCF yield carries essentially no association on its own (b = 0.56, p = 0.87), and the multivariate coefficient turns negative (−6.81, p = 0.31). The study therefore reports near-contemporaneous associations, not predictive relationships.

Within-firm (fixed-effects) estimates show a negative coefficient on prior-year EPS growth (b = −0.37 to −0.44, conventional p ≤ 0.03), but it is not robust across firms. Common year effects dominate: they lift R² from 0.10 to 0.39, consistent with strong sector-wide co-movement (Pesaran cross-sectional dependence statistic CD = 2.71 on raw returns). With six firms and nine windows, the study has power only to detect large effects. A non-significant coefficient here does not show that no relationship exists.

detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly face risks that emerge, interact and spread faster than periodic riskmanagement routines were designed to interpret. detail.abstract: It is well-documented that the average market excess returns on days with FOMC announcements are significantly higher than those on other trading days (i.e., FOMC effects). Yet, the underlying mechanisms of FOMC effects are not well-understood. This paper shows that the FOMC effects are asymmetric in the cross-section. We find that overpriced stocks, measured by high short interest, earn up to 63% (annualized) higher returns than other stocks around FOMC announcement days. The returns of these stocks reverse within half a year. The pattern is not observed during the pre-Greenspan period or in other macroeconomic announcements. We test two important channels indicating that FOMC announcements may impede short sellers from attacking overpricing. First, short squeeze dramatically intensifies on announcement days, which deters short sellers from shorting. Second, short constraints also increase. Using the short legs of 105 anomalies as an alternative proxy for overpricing, we find similar results. Overall, our results enhance our understanding of why FOMC announcements affect stock returns and whether and how the Fed may exacerbate overpricing.

detail.abstract:
Generative AI is already reshaping legal practice, and law schools that ignore it or ban it outright risk graduating students who are unprepared to use it and unable to supervise it. We propose a middle path built around two empirically backed observations. First, to use AI effectively and ethically and to mitigate AI's cognitive risks, students must build sufficient expertise to supervise AI systems the same way lawyers supervise non-lawyer colleagues in practice. Second, because AI is rapidly displacing much of the traditional legal work used to train junior lawyers, law schools must prepare graduates to enter the legal workforce at a more advanced level than in the past, including with the ability to supervise AI as part of their practice.

Building on these observations, we recommend that law schools (1) allow student use of AI on course assessments only after students have demonstrated baseline expertise without it, most fundamentally in the 1L year, though also across the entire law school curriculum; (2) permit AI as a study aid-along the lines of a "tutor" model-outside the classroom but not during class participation; (3) label every course assessment as either human-only-taken without devices or in secure exam software-or AI-assisted-in which students have the option to use AI if they also document and describe how they supervised the tools they used; (4) encourage lawyering programs, clinics, externships, labs, and simulation courses as well as pertinent cocurriculars to become a specialized training ground for ethical AI supervision where students can engage with the opportunities and risks of AI in situ under the supervision of practicing faculty; and (5) implement this framework through a standing committee, a formal learning outcome under ABA Standard 302, and a one-year pilot that is evaluated before any school-wide adoption. That committee could also review the possible risks and benefits of new uses of AI in teaching and assessment.

As we hope these recommendations make clear, we think that only faculty who are interested in using AI in their courses and assessments should do so, and those who are not should not feel pressured to. Still, as AI becomes part of practice, each instructor should at least make a deliberate choice, weighing the learning value to students (and, in clinics, to current and future clients) against any ethical or pedagogical objections, rather than leaving the question unaddressed. A few proposals, such as labeling each assessment and setting a default rule when a syllabus is silent, would apply to every course; the rest are offered as considerations for faculty who choose to engage with AI.

detail.abstract: Food banks invest heavily in collecting surplus food from grocery retailers, and food recovery policy assumes that donated food is food diverted from landfill. We test both premises using store-level records from two organizations that collect from the same 71 grocery stores without coordinating: a waste hauler, which weighs the waste it removes, and a food bank, which records the donations it collects. Because each organization records volume only when it visits, we develop a measurement framework for asynchronous pickup data that places both streams on a common footing. We exploit two sources of variation in food bank service. In our primary design, federal holidays cancel food bank collections only at stores whose regular pickup falls on the holiday's weekday. Comparing stores within the same holiday week, a holiday on the pickup day lengthens the time since the last collection by 2.2 days (35%), a result that survives placebo, balance, and randomization-inference tests. Donations fall by an estimated 31-36%. Observational data suggest that routine delays mainly shift when food is collected rather than how much, a pattern partly driven by the food bank returning sooner when stores have more product. Using long food bank service gaps as instruments, we estimate how much waste falls when donations rise. Weak-instrument-robust confidence sets exclude one-for-one diversion in the primary specification and in samples where waste is measured most reliably, and they never exclude zero: in these specifications, each additional pound donated displaces at most 0.35-0.90 pounds of recorded waste. Comparisons of 3-and 6-cubic-yard bins rule out capacity censoring as an explanation. The results imply that collection reliability matters for recovered volume and that donation volumes overstate landfill diversion.

detail.abstract: Taking the law of profit equalization as its steady-state anchor and combining it with the cost-push price transmission mechanism, this paper constructs a unified analytical framework of "housing prices-housing costsproduction and living costs-society-wide prices-household consumption behavior-macroeconomic steady state" to answer how rising housing prices push up prices across the whole economy while simultaneously suppressing domestic demand. The study proposes the hypothesis of "bidirectional anchoring by housing costs": when housing costs rise persistently and sharply, the economy is transmitted along the path of "rising rents-rising labor costs-cost stacking along the entire industrial chain-systematic price increases," and, through the sequence of interest rates, public finance, and money supply, is pushed toward severe inflation; when housing costs fall persistently, the same chain runs in reverse and the economy slides into deflation and negative interest rates. Bidirectional empirical samples from Zimbabwe, Venezuela, Iran, Russia, and Japan support this hypothesis: excessive money issuance is neither a sufficient condition nor the trigger of severe inflation, but a derivative outcome of runaway housing costs. Based on micro-level data such as the People's Bank of China Urban Depositor Survey and cross-national comparisons, this paper further argues that high housing prices induce consumption resistance and entrench weak domestic demand through a systematic mismatch between prices and labor value, and proposes a policy path centered on reducing housing costs and re-anchoring the price-to-income ratio within a reasonable range.

detail.abstract: Modern artificial intelligence can generate explanations, recommendations, and proposed actions with remarkable fluency. In consequential environments, however, the central engineering problem extends beyond producing an answer: organizations must preserve the evidence supporting a decision, distinguish facts from hypotheses, establish which properties of the decision process can be checked, react when underlying evidence changes, and recover through controlled, reviewable transitions. This paper presents Noesis Continuum, an independently designed decision-continuity architecture connecting an evidence-centered graph substrate (GraphOS), bounded goal-directed exploration and hypothesis evaluation (Labyrinth), scope-bound decision and transition verification (BAPT), constraint-based recovery planning using CP-SAT, declared-future continuity analysis (BAPT-F), and an operational Decision Database and Decision Watch. The resulting approach treats a decision not as a transient output but as a versioned, evidence-linked object with revisable justification, verification artifacts, and explicit accountability. We formalize the distinction between premise evidence, decision sufficiency, solver feasibility, and certificate scope; describe the implemented lifecycle and portable artifacts; and examine internal experiments, including null and negative results that motivate a pre-specified independent evaluation protocol. Noesis Continuum's central proposed contribution is the combination of verifiable decision transitions with longitudinal evidence monitoring and recovery-not a claim that verification establishes external truth or that all decisions become correct. The system provides the computational foundations on which consequential decision claims can be precisely stated, tested, contested, and revised.

detail.abstract: Governance of artificial intelligence is organised around individual systems, yet consequential outcomes increasingly arise from the way systems combine. I use interactionality to describe the condition in which interactions among technological, algorithmic and institutional systems materially shape outcomes that cannot be adequately understood by examining any system independently. Distinguishing interaction effects from governance-boundary crossings, I identify the Cross-System and Interaction-Level Accountability Gaps, alongside the Swarm Accountability Gap from earlier work. A structured comparison of eleven documented cases, drawn from judgments, regulatory orders, official inquiries and supervisory reports, shows that material interaction effects and governance-boundary crossings can be distinguished in practice. The cases also suggest that clearly assigned responsibility at governance boundaries can support accountability and remedy, while interaction-dependent outcomes may remain difficult to reconstruct or attribute. The findings are exploratory and make no causal or general claims. I review current financial supervision, discuss the economic incidence of unresolved accountability, including for financial inclusion, the Global South and women, and set out governance principles and a research agenda.

detail.abstract: We study the minimum total-variation distance between two population laws compatible with positive observed distributions, shared visible inverse capture factors, and a fixed family of separately labeled unobserved strata. Each date has its own coverage floor. Several strata can improve on the best singleton explanation for some observations exactly when the two interior floors sum to more than one. We determine the sharp supremum of this improvement at every pair of floors by reducing it to a one-variable maximization. The supremum is approached by positive binary observations but is never attained by a finite strictly positive instance in the positive-gain region. At a fixed sum of floors, balancing the floors strictly increases the envelope. The proof combines a complete opposite-pair catalogue with singleton comparisons that leave every visible factor free. An example with a vanishing shared visible cell shows why arbitrary disjoint-limit approximations need not preserve the binary sharpness behavior.

detail.abstract: An investor may possess a valid legal entitlement yet be unable to transfer, redeem, or recover the associated asset when an intermediary, registry, payment system, or legal process becomes unavailable. Its contribution is a structured method for identifying which dependencies are indispensable, which degrade performance, which are substitutable, and which remedies remain available under stress.

detail.abstract: I have spent 23 years in the rubber and plastics industry. I started in sales in January 2003, learned the business from the ground up, and today I own and run COi Rubber Products, a USowned manufacturer of custom molded rubber and plastic parts. This thesis grows out of that experience. Entrepreneurship education can build knowledge without supplying the resources a person needs to actually take part in commerce. Access to an established business can close that gap, but access alone can also create dependence and unequal chances to keep the value a person helps create. I develop a framework I call shared commercial infrastructure (SCI): an arrangement that links structured learning, governed access to a company's commercial resources, and real market-facing practice. Drawing on research on human capital, learning transfer, relational resources, effectuation, and power dependence, I separate outcomes that are often blurred together: capability, commercial activity, sponsor performance, participant net income, and durable economic options. My central argument is simple. Lowering the barrier to entry does not by itself close the gap between creating value and keeping a fair share of it. Eight propositions specify the roles of instructional complementarity, calibrated feedback, network access, compensation governance, payment timing, portability, capacity, and incentives. My own company's developing representative program, the Purple Team, serves as a motivating illustration, not as evidence of effectiveness. I propose comparative research designs, participant-level accounting, distributional measures, and independent governance that could identify benefits, null results, and harms. The contribution is a conditional model of inclusive commercial participation, not a claim that shared infrastructure automatically democratizes entrepreneurship.

detail.abstract: Background: Recognition and reward practices are considered central to public-sector human resource management, yet the correspondence among performance-contingent awards, innovation rewards, and recognition of high-quality work remains underexplored at the federal agency level. Objective: This study examined the agency-level associations of perceived performance-contingent awards and innovation rewards with perceived recognition of high-quality products and services. Methods: Secondary cross-sectional ecological analysis was conducted on 36 non-overlapping U.S. federal agency-level observations selected from 44 supplied aggregate records. Three item-level agency means represented award contingency (Item 25), innovation rewards (Item 32), and quality-related recognition (Item 31). Pearson and Spearman correlations, ordinary least squares (OLS) multiple regression, hierarchical regression, HC3 heteroscedasticityconsistent inference, and influence diagnostics were used. Results: Agency mean recognition correlated positively with award contingency (r = .916) and innovation rewards (r = .967). The simultaneous model explained 96.5% of between-agency variation (R² = .965, adjusted R² = .963; F[2, 33] = 461.60, p < .001). Both associations persisted under HC3 inference (Item 25: B = .409, p = .001; Item 32: B = .667, p < .001). Adding innovation rewards after award contingency increased R² by .126, whereas the converse increment was .030. A Breusch-Pagan test indicated heteroscedasticity (p = .017). Conclusion: Agencies with higher ratings of both reward practices also reported higher recognition of high-quality work, with innovation rewards providing the larger unique association. Because the data are contemporaneous perceptions aggregated to agencies, results are descriptive and associational rather than causal or employee-level.

detail.abstract: In today's highly competitive business environment, employee retention has become a strategic imperative, particularly as organizations struggle with high turnover driven in part by ineffective conflict management systems. This study examines the influence of conflict management styles on employee retention, drawing on the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument and Social Exchange Theory to explain how assertiveness, collaboration, and reciprocal workplace relationships shape employee commitment and organizational stability. Employing a meta-analytic approach, this study synthesizes findings from peer-reviewed research published between 2010 and 2023, focusing on the private sector. It integrates insights from both qualitative and quantitative studies to assess the relationship between specific conflict management styles integrating, compromising, dominating, avoiding, and accommodating and employee retention. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity tests were conducted to assess the consistency of results across different industries and organizational settings. The results indicate that integrating and accommodating conflict styles are consistently linked to higher employee retention and job satisfaction, with effect sizes ranging from r = 0.38 to β = 0.52. In contrast, avoidance and dominating styles correlate weakly or negatively with retention due to their failure to resolve core conflicts effectively. These findings emphasize the critical role of collaborative and empathetic conflict resolution in fostering long-term workforce stability. The study concludes that effective conflict management is essential for sustaining employee loyalty and organizational resilience. The study recommends that managers should proactively identify potential conflict areas and adopt context-appropriate strategies. Future research should employ mixed methods to fill methodological gaps and support evidence-based human resource practices.

detail.abstract: Clean Air Act nonattainment imposes higher costs on entrants than incumbents, which may induce incumbents to strategically increase pollution to deter entry and strengthen market power. Consistent with this, during the 1997 PM2.5 standards' nonattainment-determination window, ex-ante near-nonattainment-threshold firms increased emissions relative to those slightly away. detail.abstract: The digital transformation of firms is increasingly recognized as a key driver of competitiveness and resilience, yet significant disparities remain-especially among SMEs and traditional manufacturing regions. This study provides an initial, exploratory assessment of the digital maturity of firms in the Marche region of Italy, a territory characterized by a dense network of district-based SMEs and strong specialization in traditional industries. Although based on the limited set of Digital Maturity Assessments (DMAs) collected so far, the analysis offers valuable early insights into the starting conditions of firms that voluntarily approached the regional European Digital Innovation Hub, EDIH4MARCHE. Digital readiness is measured through the DMA framework developed by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre, which captures technological, organizational, and strategic aspects of digitalization. The study examines variations in digital maturity across firm size and sector and applies complementary analytical techniques to identify emerging patterns within the available data. Despite the preliminary nature of the dataset, results highlight clear trends: microfirms and companies in traditional sectors tend to display lower levels of digital maturity, while medium-sized firms and those operating in more technology-intensive industries show comparatively higher readiness. These early findings provide a useful foundation for future, more comprehensive analyses as additional data become available, and they offer initial indications on where targeted policy and support actions may be most needed to accelerate SMEs' transition toward Industry 4.0.

detail.abstract: An arbitration agreement cannot be assumed to be governed by the law governing the contract in which it sits. By reason of the separability principle, it is independent of the other terms, and the parties' choice of the proper law of the contract does not determine the validity of the arbitration clause — a point confirmed by the Supreme People's Court in a 2006 reply and illustrated by divergence among jurisdictions, notably the Singapore Court of Appeal's decision in BCY v. BCZ [2017] 3 SLR 357 and the contrasting English authorities. The essay sets out the mainland Chinese conflicts rules in force in 2017 — the 2006 Judicial Interpretation on the Arbitration Law (Art. 16), the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign‑Related Civil Relations (Art. 18) and the First Judicial Interpretation on that Law (Art. 14) — and shows, by a hypothetical SIAC clause, how a mainland court and a Singapore court may each apply the other's law, "the courtesy of gentlemen" (谦谦君子之交). It then raises the unresolved question whether "the law of the place of the arbitral institution or the law of the seat" in Art. 18 should be read in the order written or in favour of validity. Finally it describes the reporting system for rulings that an arbitration agreement is invalid, and observes that the system necessarily also reviews the choice‑of‑law question. The 2026 Notes record that the validity‑preferring answer was supplied by judicial interpretation in 2018, that the First Judicial Interpretation was renumbered in 2020, and that the revised Arbitration Law of 2026 has made the seat the governing connecting factor.

detail.abstract: Various case studies have highlighted the positive economic effects of artisanal mining, while also raising concerns about potential negative social effects, particularly those associated with informal mines. We analyse the net impact of informal artisanal gold mines in Burkina Faso on expenditure, wealth, health and education of neighbouring households. We use household surveys, the location of 2,277 artisanal mines and high-resolution satellite images to determine the date on which the mines began operating. We also differentiate between formal and informal artisanal mines. We find that artisanal mining increases household expenditure by 10-20%, while wealth accumulation is limited to 6-10%. Artisanal mining improves school attendance by 2.2 percentage points and reduces infant mortality by 1.5-3.3 percentage points. However, we observe substantial increases in spending on alcohol and tobacco, by 30-40%. The formalisation of mines correlates with higher household expenditure, but also with higher expenditure on temptation goods.

detail.abstract:
A consumer using an AI assistant for free generates no subscription revenue, yet each interaction carries a real cost. Deutsche Bank analysts estimate that the free tier of Meta's Muse assistant, at 100 million AI tokens per week, probably costs Meta about $40 per user per month.[1] The scale of the bet is now documented: within six weeks of launch, more than 10 million people in the United States and Canada set up Muse agents, Meta's quarterly capital expenditure reached $34.9 billion, and quarterly free cash flow turned negative.[2, 3] Because substantially all of Meta's revenue is advertising-$196.2 billion of $201.0 billion in 2025[4]the plausible financing mechanism is the one familiar from multisided platforms: one group is subsidised because its participation creates value for paying groups.[5] 

This paper assembles the documented evidence, separates it from hypotheses and illustrative calculations, and asks three linked questions. First, who ultimately bears the cost of a free assistant? The paper's central answer is that everyone does, whether or not they use the product. Users pay in stated intention; family members and contacts pay in data inferred from other people's behaviour; non-users pay through tracking on third-party websites and "shadow" contact data assembled from address books they never uploaded; advertisers pay price premiums; consumers at large may pay through retail price pass-through; and capital markets fund the deficit while the recovery paths are tested. Second, what does the platform capture in exchange-specifically, Meta's announced use of AI-chat interactions as an advertising personalisation signal from 16 December 2025?[6, 7] Third, what new risks does concentrating identity, relationships, purchase intention, and increasingly sensitive conversation data in one place create-including the catastrophic tail case in which a security breach or AI-specific attack exposes that aggregation? 

The argument is analytical rather than accusatory. Meta's documented record-the Cambridge Analytica misuse of data on 87 million users, the publication of scraped data on 533 million people, the record €1.2 billion GDPR fine, more than $200 million in healthcare-tracking settlements, and the €805 million Italian camera-roll fine of November 2026-establishes that platform-scale data concentration has repeatedly produced documented harm, giving the security question empirical weight rather than speculative character. The conclusion frames the central governance question for managers and regulators alike: a free assistant can be a genuine bargain, but only if the incentives of the party financing it remain transparent, the people financ-Preprint. detail.abstract: The Donabedian model of structure, process, and outcome is a framework on which much research on the quality of care rests, but the body of research that relies on it has not been mapped across databases. This study maps the records that name Donabedian in PubMed and Scopus and asks how the name serves the studies that use it. Records with "Donabedian" in the title, abstract, or keywords were retrieved (858 from PubMed and 1,097 from Scopus, 1975–2025), matched by PubMed identifier or DOI, and analyzed with bibliometrix in R; every occurrence of the name in abstracts was located by rule. PubMed contained 77.1% of the Scopus records in the medical subject areas; those it lacked were mostly nursing and general practice journals in Chinese, Portuguese, and Spanish. The noun after the name was "model" in 20.5% of the occurrences up to 2000 and 46.1% in 2015–2025. In a subset matched to an earlier Scopus study, counts by country depended on the counting unit: the United States had 182 of 622 articles by first author, against 764 author–country pairs. Donabedian's approaches to assessment became a named model that studies cite as the framework of their methods, and a review of this research needs Scopus as well as PubMed.

detail.abstract: Policy uncertainty and financial market stress jointly shape downside risks to UK GDP, but which of the two dominates changes over time. Using an SV-BVAR on UK monthly data, this paper documents two empirical findings. First, the attribution of GDP tail risk to uncertainty versus financial stress depends on how structural shocks are identified: across five recursive (Cholesky) orderings the implied contributions fan out and can misattribute which source drives a given episode, whereas order-invariant identification (OINV) pins down a single, economically coherent decomposition. Second, the composition of tail risk is time-varying: policy uncertainty explains a smoother and often larger share of GDP forecast-risk variation, while financial stress drives the strongest realized downside contributions in crises, so that uncertainty-led episodes (Brexit, the 2025 tariff shock) are distinct from stress-led ones (the Global Financial Crisis, the 2022 LDI episode). Supporting out-of-sample evidence shows that the stochastic-volatility BVAR, and in particular its Student-t extension, ranks lower-tail outcomes more accurately than parsimonious Growth-at-Risk quantile regressions, even when the latter are given the model's full information set.

detail.abstract: This paper experimentally investigates how auction format and selling structure affect bidding behavior, revenue, and efficiency in multi-unit auctions. Using laboratory markets in which two identical units are sold, we compare Dutch and English clock auctions under both simultaneous and sequential selling formats, while varying market thickness between three-and five-bidder environments. Under risk-neutral Bayesian Nash equilibrium, these institutions are predicted to generate equivalent revenue and efficiency. The experimental results reveal systematic behavioral departures from these predictions. In Dutch auctions, bidders frequently overbid relative to equilibrium benchmarks, particularly in thinner three-bidder markets, generating revenues substantially above theoretical predictions. In contrast, bidders in English auctions tend to underbid, especially in simultaneous formats, resulting in revenues below equilibrium benchmarks. Sequential selling mitigates underbidding in English auctions and reproduces the wellknown declining-price anomaly in both Dutch and English settings. Despite these behavioral differences, all auction formats achieve high efficiency, with English auctions being slightly more efficient on average. Overall, the simultaneous Dutch auction generates the highest revenues, while English auctions produce marginally greater efficiency. The findings demonstrate that auction institution and market thickness jointly shape the consequences of behavioral departures from equilibrium, suggesting that revenue and efficiency outcomes in multi-unit auctions depend critically on the interaction between auction rules and bidder behavior.

detail.abstract: The expansion of clean-energy technologies, AI-related industries, and advanced defense technologies has increased the strategic importance of critical minerals. Much of the discussion on mineral security has focused on access to deposits, mining rights, and bilateral trade. This paper examines another stage of the supply chain: the processing and refining of minerals after extraction. This midstream stage can create significant dependencies even when countries have secured access to mineral resources. The paper examines India as a case study, focusing on its import dependence for selected critical minerals and the concentration of processing and refining capacity among major trading partners. Using international trade data and supply-chain analysis, it assesses the extent to which dependence at the processing stage can create vulnerabilities for India's clean-energy and strategic industries. Conceptually, the paper draws on the idea of "weaponized interdependence" and research on minilateral cooperation to develop the concept of Midstream Zone Balancing. The concept refers to cooperation among states to diversify processing capacity rather than relying solely on access to upstream mineral resources. Such cooperation could involve locating processing facilities in resource-producing partner countries, joint investment and financing arrangements, and long-term supply agreements.

detail.abstract: We ask whether merger remedies that facilitate a competitor's entry protect consumers. detail.abstract: We study how different institutions governing property rights and economic transactions shape occupational choices and welfare. Individuals in our society choose occupations that determine their production and consumption opportunities, anticipating either anonymous, voluntary market exchange supported by public enforcement (the market), or allocations through a random coercive hierarchy (the jungle) without monetary compensation. We establish conditions for occupational equilibria to exist in the market and in the jungle, and compare their performance. At a common occupational profile, the market maximizes aggregate surplus, whereas allocations in the jungle are Pareto efficient with monetary holdings fixed but need not maximize surplus. Endogenous occupational choices introduce an additional source of institutional differences. We find that a market occupational equilibrium outperforms a jungle occupational equilibrium, in aggregate terms, under two conditions: (i) every occupation in the jungle is available in the market, and (ii) the market is perfectly competitive, in the sense that prices cannot be manipulated by unilateral changes in occupations. We also establish an individual welfare comparison without this price-invariance condition: among identical individuals, everyone weakly prefers an occupational equilibrium in the market to a symmetric occupational equilibrium in the jungle. Our analysis places the institutional foundations of exchange at the center of the welfare comparison and provides a framework for studying coercive institutions that survive alongside markets.

detail.abstract: Institutional investors increasingly act as landlords in private rental housing markets, a trend frequently linked to rising prices and 'bad landlord behavior'. Yet systematic quantitative assessments connecting institutional ownership to either outcome remain rare, particularly in the European context. To test both dimensions, we construct a panel of all private rental plots in Vienna for 2010-2022, classifying landlords by linking land registry, building registry, and company databases, applying different institutional investor definitions. We first merge several indicators of 'bad landlord behavior', short-and long-term vacancy, overcharging on rents and utilities, and poor maintenance, to estimate extended two-way fixed effects (ETWFE) differencein-differences models. We find no significant effect across all outcomes and specifications, challenging simple narratives of institutional investors as universally 'bad landlords'. We then merge property-level sales prices onto the ownership panel to assess institutional takeovers and exits from a financial perspective. Hedonic regressions show that institutional investors enter at prices comparable to other owners but sell at significantly higher ones. Consistent with this, repeated-sales regressions indicate that institutional investors who both enter and exit within the study period earn significantly higher annualized gross returns than other owners. Despite limited means of controlling for qualitative improvements, these results suggest that institutional investors have contributed to Vienna's substantial real estate price increases, either through buy-fix-sell strategies or through exercising of market power.

detail.abstract: Voluntary and compliance carbon markets frequently suffer from price volatility, greenwashing incentives, and compliance default when abatement costs escalate unexpectedly. Conventional cap-and-trade architectures rely on static emissions caps and rigid punitive fines, which often induce industrial firms to misreport abatement progress or exit green supply chain commitments during macroeconomic downturns. detail.abstract: A node lock fixes one player's strategy at a single decision and asks what the restriction costs. This note separates the direct cost D of a lock, with every other policy held at the reference, from the total cost C after all three seats re-solve, in a 40 bb three-player postflop spot solved with discounted counterfactual regret minimisation. In an archived panel of 53 locks on J♥9♦8♦, built by moving first the hands that lose least from the move, the residual A = C − D accounts for 89% and 71% of summed cost for ±10 and ±20 percentage-point moves, but one lock carries 45% of the ±10 pp total and the median lock-level shares are 81% and 73%. The opponents' unilateral best-response gains exceed C for every archived lock, about tenfold at the median. Version 1.1 adds runs whose analysis was fixed before they were made. When the same aggregate move is spread over all hands or made with hands in random order, summed D rises about fourfold. In five re-solves with these constructions, C changes in both directions; for the dominant lock it falls from 0.395 bb to 0.0007 bb, too small to distinguish from zero in these solves. A small direct cost is therefore a property of the lock construction, not of node locking in general; in the five re-solves, C and its split into D and A also change with the construction. With opponents held at the reference, the locked player's own re-optimisation avoids 77–87% of summed D on J♥9♦8♦, mostly by reaching the locked node less often. The results describe these locks in one modelled spot. The note, its data bundle and the solver source code are deposited at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24212415).

detail.abstract: This study examined the relationship of praise, public commendation, and monetary incentives with self-reported motivation, work performance, and job satisfaction among employees of the Local Government Unit of Talisayan, Misamis Oriental. A quantitative, cross-sectional correlational design was used. The study included 126 employees (71 permanent and 55 casual) and employed an adopted and modified four-point Likert-type questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and Pearson product-moment correlations were used. Praise (M = 3.51), public commendation (M = 3.42), and monetary incentives (M = 3.40) were rated Highly Practiced. Motivation (M = 3.51), job satisfaction (M = 3.51), and work performance (M = 3.49) were rated Very High. Praise and public commendation each showed significant, weak positive correlations with all three outcomes (r = .235-.334). Monetary incentives were significantly associated with work performance (r = .279, p = .002) and job satisfaction (r = .218, p = .014), but not with motivation (r = .163, p = .068). Eight of nine correlations were statistically significant at α = .05. Non-monetary recognition exhibited a more consistent pattern of significant associations; the design does not support causal conclusions. The findings offer local evidence for reviewing recognition practices alongside other determinants of employee outcomes.

detail.abstract: Assistive technology can raise productivity, but how does unequal access shape judgments of deservingness? detail.abstract: Between November 2015 and February 2024 the Government of India sold 146.96 tonnes of gold-denominated debt to households under the Sovereign Gold Bond scheme, raising ₹72,274 crore. Using data on all 67 tranches, I measure the cost of this borrowing against the conventional bonds issued at the same time. The 24 tranches that have matured cost 15.2% a year on average, against a 7.1% yield on 10-year government bonds at issue. About 122.8 tonnes remain outstanding, with a redemption value of ₹1.72 lakh crore at the 16 November 2026 reference price of ₹14,024 a gram, against ₹65,150 crore raised. If gold holds that price (a scenario, not a forecast), the scheme will have cost about ₹75,800 crore more than conventional borrowing, slightly more than the amount raised; the estimate ranges from ₹34,300 crore if gold falls 30% to ₹1.27 lakh crore if it rises 10% a year. Much of this was foreseeable from the historical record. The coupon was worth about 15% of proceeds at issue and is hard to justify on pricing grounds, and the scheme could undercut conventional debt only if rupee gold rose by less than about 4.7% a year, which it had done in fewer than one in five 8-year windows between 1981 and 2015. Roughly a quarter of the growth in the liability reflects rupee depreciation. I discuss hedging counterfactuals, the offset from the Reserve Bank of India's gold purchases, and the design of any successor scheme.

detail.abstract: Written mine safety controls may be formally complete, but they may be misunderstood, unavailable, or inconsistently enacted. Injury rates are retrospective, training completion does not demonstrate control competence, climate scores measure perceptions, and audit closure does not prove that a fatal risk barrier performs during normal work. This conceptual article proposes a role-stratified diagnostic for critical control implementation and a six-phase experimental roadmap. It combines a Safety Control Competence Index (SCCI), independently observed Control Enactment Rate (CER), critical control verification, non-compensatory control failure and misconception flags, and hazard-specific exposure. The continuous implementation strength is and the deficit is ; the symmetric geometric mean represents two jointly necessary conditions, while validated conjunctive thresholds are retained for operational decisions. Absolute divergence is paired with its signed direction to distinguish competence, work design, resources, and supervision pathways. The protocol specifies genuine observation opportunities, binomial precision targets, Hawthorne effect controls, contractor and language equity, CER comparability conditions, Indian legal and ethical safeguards, pilot-versus-definitive propositions, provisional smallest effects of scientific interest, and an implementation burden model. The initial study was a feasibility and measurement pilot, not a fatality reduction test or regulatory rating. A hypothetical underground coal example was used to illustrate the calculations without the effects of claims. The intended contribution is a testable bridge between critical control assurance and evidence regarding whether role-specific controls are understood and enacted in the field.

detail.abstract: Employment contracts provide an important framework for organizing paid work and recognizing workers' rights, including access to social insurance. However, formal employment does not necessarily guarantee social security protection. This study examines social security non-entitlement among formal-sector employees in Ghana using the Annual Household Income and Expenditure Survey (AHIES) for 2022-2024. We apply survey-weighted linear probability models with standard errors clustered at the enumeration-area level. The results show that private-sector employees have a 14.19-percentage-point higher adjusted prevalence of reported non-entitlement than public-sector employees (95% CI: 10.30-18.08). Age exhibits a nonlinear association with non-entitlement, while permanent and full-time employment are associated with significantly lower prevalence. Occupational composition explains only a small share of the public-private difference. The adjusted gap is 17.04 percentage points in 2022, 11.99 in 2023 and 13.78 in 2024. A joint Wald test finds no statistically significant variation across the years (p = 0.295), indicating that the disparity persisted throughout the study period. Non-entitlement also overlaps with the absence of paid sick or maternity leave, revealing multiple gaps in employment protection. These findings point to the need for stronger monitoring of social security entitlement in formal employment, particularly in the private sector.

detail.abstract: Rational choice neo-institutionalism explains how science transforms the self-interested actions of individual researchers into reliable public knowledge through constitutional, distributive, and aggregative rules (Shi, 2001). However, this framework assumed exclusively human cognitive agency and a clear separation between non-market academic credit and commercial property regimes. The rise of autonomous AI agents and proprietary foundation models destabilises that institutional equilibrium. This paper extends the neo-institutionalist theory of science to AImediated research by reconceptualising constitutional rules as a three-tier governance hierarchy: (1) an epistemic and technical constitution, where cognitive paradigms merge with AI system architectures ("code as law"); (2) an institutional constitution, allocating authority, residual control rights, and liability across a tripartite principal–agent structure comprising the scientific entrepreneur, the AI system owner, and the delegated artificial agent; and (3) an operational regime of Human-in-the-Loop mandates, audit standards, and technical guardrails. Analysing how zeromarginal-cost AI outputs and black-box information asymmetry induce peer-review congestion, adverse selection, and epistemic monoculture in the intellectual market, the paper outlines concrete constitutional reforms for funding agencies, universities, and journals to realign incentives and safeguard evolutionary selection in automated discovery.

detail.abstract: We develop an integrated framework to quantify the short-run impacts of carbon pricing on climate and air pollution externalities in the electricity sector. Combining machine learning and chemical transport modeling, we track policy impacts all the way from electricity dispatch and emissions of CO2 and air pollutants at the generating unit to formation of secondary PM2.5, population exposure and associated premature deaths. Using hourly data from 732 fossil generating units in 13 European countries, we estimate that carbon pricing under the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) reduced CO 2 emissions by 5.7% between 2016 and 2021. The abatement channel is coal-to-gas substitution which occurs within and between interconnected electricity markets. Carbon pricing reduces PM2.5-related mortality due to co-emissions by 8.9%. Monetized health co-benefits exceed the incremental generation costs by more than e 5 billion, implying a net welfare increase in Europe on top of global climate benefits. Counterfactual analyses reveal that net co-benefits per tonne amount to 60% of what is feasible with socially optimal pollution taxes, and that marginal co-benefits are weakly decreasing in the permit price. Overall, our results reinforce the role of cap-and-trade as an efficient policy instrument to internalize both carbon and air pollution externalities of power generation.

detail.abstract: Having children is widely expected to make investors more cautious, and suitability questionnaires routinely collect information on dependants. Using a purpose-built survey of 1,549 investors in Finland, Germany, Italy and Spain, we apply an Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition to the gap in selfreported financial risk taking between parents and non-parents. The small and statistically insignificant raw gap conceals two components of opposite sign: parents' observable profile, above all their older age, is associated with less risk taking (-0.27 points on a 1-7 scale), whereas, among investors with the same characteristics, parents report taking more risk than non-parents (+0.38 points). This conditional parenthood gap is robust to alternative covariates, estimators and samples, and to sensitivity analyses for unobserved confounding and for the association between parenthood and the decision to invest. It is larger for mothers than for fathers, so that the gender gap in risk taking is narrower among parents than among non-parents. In an out-of-sample profiling exercise, a demographic profile that ignores parenthood assigns about one third of mothers to a lower risk class than the one they report, and treating parenthood as a signal of caution makes this error larger. Parenthood thus conveys information on investors' risk taking beyond standard demographic characteristics, with implications for how suitability assessments weigh risk tolerance against the capacity to bear losses.

detail.abstract: Our stochastic-mechanical research programme (Andreev & Howden, 2026a) claimed that signals derived from a Bohmian and quantum-field-theoretic reading of market dynamics carry predictive information about forward returns, variance, and regime transitions. Those signals included a crash probability computed from a tunnelling (instanton) action and the spontaneous-symmetry-breaking condensate |Φ|² (the squared order parameter of a model of changes in factor structure). The others were the decoherence rate (the rate at which the leading eigenvectors of the return correlation matrix rotate between successive windows), the osmotic velocity of the Nelson decomposition (the order-flow component of drift), and path signatures (iterated-integral summaries of a price path). We registered each claim before scoring it, with its thresholds and primary outcome fixed in advance (a frozen protocol), and evaluated it at the Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016) multiple-testing bar (t > 3). Of the eight registered claims in Table 1, none is confirmed at the registered bar under its frozen protocol. Seven are settled null or disconfirmed: five of the six that concern forward returns or crash timing, the one on forward variance, and the one on a relation between signals. On forward variance the signals degraded a HAR-RV + ln(VIX) baseline, a heterogeneous autoregressive model of realised variance augmented with the log of the VIX (Diebold-Mariano t = −1.69 on 1,861 out-of-sample days, 2019-2026). The eighth, the instanton crash-timing claim, is not confirmed, and its prospective protocol is unscored: its statistic of 4.66 falls to roughly 1.5-1.9 once the overlap in its forward windows is accounted for, and no significance is claimed for an in-sample re-test on 9,743 days from 1987 to 2025 (Table 1, first row) until the prospective sample its protocol requires has been collected and scored. With no claim confirmed, we demote physics from predictor to (i) a mechanics model of two-way spot-options feedback, which Black-Scholes structurally omits (the self-consistent dealer-flow field; Andreev & Howden, 2026f), and (ii) an orthogonality and estimation role: a signal overlap matrix that is, by exact identity, a Fisher information matrix and a density matrix (Andreev & Howden, 2026l), together with the estimation methods that survived audit (random-matrix covariance cleaning, higher-moment tensors). In its reformulated form the programme makes narrower, falsifiable, mechanism-level claims and abandons the broad predictive one. The null results are reported from the project's own register of hypotheses.
