detail.abstract:
How can a hospital continue to correct care when the cause of an infectious event is still unknown, staff and services are under pressure, and independent review may later be needed?

This article introduces Joint Clinical and Evidentiary Viability (JCEV), a framework for examining those responsibilities together. It asks whether a health service can act in time to protect patients while preserving a lawful possibility of independent review, using the staff, resources, and authority actually available.

The article’s contribution is deliberately bounded. JCEV is an integrated framework for assessment, not a new mathematical method or a validated score. It proposes a testable signal, joint failure under binding rules: a schedule may be physically possible, yet no allocation may comply with the legal obligations or formally adopted institutional rules that govern the facility and decision. The article sets out how future studies could distinguish this result from an ordinary shortage of staff or capacity, and from problems already identified by standard scheduling methods.

Historical and contemporary cases, including antimicrobial resistance in India, Ebola in West Africa, COVID related pressures in conflict affected settings, Sverdlovsk, and earlier warfare, show how infection can expose weaknesses in care, staffing, trust, and coordination. These cases provide context; they do not validate JCEV or establish that an event was deliberate.

The analysis brings together biotechnology and clinical diagnostics, health service resilience, international humanitarian law, public health obligations, and questions of accountability. It is intended for readers working in health security, public health, international law, biosecurity, and the resilience of medical services.

detail.abstract: In today's highly competitive global manufacturing landscape, organizations continuously seek robust approaches to enhance product quality, streamline operational processes, and achieve sustainable cost efficiency. Six Sigma has emerged as a data-driven systematic methodology designed to eliminate defects, minimize process variations, and improve overall operational performance. This research investigates the application of Six Sigma methodologies specifically DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control) in production operations and evaluates its effects on defect reduction and cost optimization. The study adopts a mixed-method research design, combining quantitative performance data analysis with qualitative insights from manufacturing practitioners. Findings reveal that systematic implementation of Six Sigma significantly reduces defect rates, leading to substantial savings in rework, scrap, warranty, and operational costs. However, successful implementation requires strong leadership commitment, adequate training, cultural alignment, and sustained organizational support. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge on quality management practices and provides empirical evidence guiding manufacturing organizations in designing and executing effective Six Sigma initiatives.

detail.abstract: Educational institutions are increasingly expected to move beyond conventional knowledge transmission towards developing individuals capable of generating new knowledge, creating intellectual property, designing innovative solutions and addressing complex societal challenges. In this context, strategic innovation and strategic thinking provide important foundations for transforming educational institutions into environments that systematically develop inventive, design-oriented, creative and problem-solving capabilities. This article proposes an integrated institutional framework for developing an Intellectual Property (IP) Portfolio comprising both institutional and student-generated intellectual assets through the systematic development of innovative mindsets, pedagogical practices, research capabilities and organisational culture. The central argument is that intellectual property development should not be treated merely as a legal, commercial or administrative activity. Rather, it should become an educational outcome emerging from the continuous development of inventive thinking, design thinking, creative thinking, critical thinking and problem-solving thinking. Students should be encouraged to identify opportunities, recognise unmet needs, investigate challenges, generate original ideas, develop prototypes, experiment with alternatives, validate solutions, document their contributions and transform promising outputs into protectable intellectual assets. The article proposes a strategic framework connecting five dimensions: (1) strategic innovation in educational institutions; (2) strategic thinking and mindset development; (3) inventive, design, creative and problem-solving pedagogies; (4) institutional and student intellectual property portfolio development; and (5) the establishment of a sustainable culture of innovation. It also examines the institutional responsibilities associated with intellectual property ownership, student rights, research collaboration, commercialisation, technology transfer, interdisciplinary learning and innovation assessment. The article concludes that an educational institution's long-term innovation capacity depends not simply on the number of patents, publications, products or start-ups it produces, but on its ability to create a sustainable intellectual ecosystem in which every student becomes a potential knowledge creator, inventor, designer, researcher and problem solver.

detail.abstract: Immunosuppressive therapies are essential for the management of autoimmune disorders, organ transplantation, and malignant disease, but they may alter host defense and increase susceptibility to serious infection. Although patients receiving these agents may require antibiotic therapy more often in selected clinical settings, increased infection susceptibility does not justify routine or indiscriminate antibiotic use. This narrative review examines the immunologic basis of infection risk, summarizes observational and trial-based evidence, and considers implications for empirical treatment, antimicrobial prophylaxis, and stewardship. In a population-based cohort, oral glucocorticoid exposure was associated with higher risks of cellulitis and lower respiratory tract infection. A meta-analysis of rheumatoid arthritis trials also identified dose-dependent differences in serious infection risk with biological agents. Importantly, these studies assessed infection outcomes rather than a universal need for additional antibiotic courses. Current guidance supports prompt empirical antibacterial treatment for febrile neutropenia and targeted prophylaxis for narrowly defined high-risk groups, alongside microbiological reassessment, de-escalation, and infection prevention. A risk-adapted strategy-rather than automatic escalation of antibiotic frequency, dose, or duration-offers the most defensible approach to infection management in immunosuppressed adults.

detail.abstract: The Philippine service industry, including hospitality, retail, transport, and professional services, remains highly vulnerable to sudden disruptions such as typhoons, earthquakes, public-health emergencies, and market shocks [1]. While many large service firms have begun developing business continuity plans (BCPs), the level of business continuity readiness (BCR) and its measurable effect on organizational resilience (OR) remain under-quantified within the Philippine setting [2]. This quantitative study examined the relationship between business continuity readiness (risk assessment, crisis preparedness, continuity planning, recovery planning, and monitoring) and organizational resilience (operational resilience, strategic resilience, and adaptive resilience) among selected service-sector enterprises operating within Metro Manila, Philippines. Using a descriptive-correlational and regression research design, a total of 384 managers and operations supervisors from service industry firms responded to a validated survey instrument adapted from established business-continuity and resilience frameworks [9]. Findings revealed that business continuity readiness had a statistically significant positive effect on organizational resilience, indicating that higher continuity readiness predicts greater organizational resilience among Philippine service-industry enterprises. Specifically, crisis preparedness and recovery planning emerged as the strongest predictors of resilience. The study concludes that formal business-continuity readiness assessment should be integrated into regular organizational risk reviews for Philippine service-sector firms. A proposed resilience-continuity framework was developed as a basis for policy, training, and enterprise-level continuity-planning initiatives.

detail.abstract: The Federal Communications Commission’s 2020 framework for transitioning the 900 MHz band from narrowband land mobile radio to broadband resolved long-standing spectrum fragmentation and enabled private broadband deployment by electric utilities and other critical-infrastructure operators. This paper examines whether the same framework also created the structural conditions for durable single-firm dominance. It asks, first, to what extent the market for 900 MHz broadband licenses is concentrated in a single holder and, second, whether the Commission’s regulatory architecture allows that holder to establish supracompetitive pricing and pass costs through to ratepayers. Drawing on the Coasean tradition in spectrum policy and the entry-barrier literature of Bain and Salop, the paper analyzes the 2020 Report and Order, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau’s 2024 order (DA 24-600), the 2026 Report and Order, and Anterix’s public SEC filings. It finds that the Commission’s eligibility requirements function as a structural entry barrier favoring a single capital-intensive first mover. These requirements are majority ownership of licensed spectrum in a county, clearance of incumbents holding at least 90 percent of site-channels, and anti-windfall spectrum returns. Anterix alone satisfies the eligibility test in approximately 3,200 of 3,233 U.S. counties. Confidential transaction terms, imperfect substitutes, asymmetric bargaining, and diffuse ratepayer exposure have together prevented any countervailing check from emerging. Because confidentiality precludes direct measurement of price effects, the paper reframes competitive harm as a question of whether regulatory design renders harm probable, rather than whether observed prices deviate from a competitive benchmark. As the 2026 order extends the same architecture, the analysis bears directly on the design of future spectrum allocation frameworks.

detail.abstract: Contemporary global crises increasingly intersect, creating complex and mutually reinforcing threats to socioeconomic stability, human security, and sustainable development. The book series Socioeconomic Challenges Amidst a Global Triple Threat of Conflicts, COVID-19, and Climate Change, a multidisciplinary, sevenvolume scholarly work that explores the interconnected consequences of the three crises, collectively termed the "3Cs." Drawing on diverse national and regional experiences, the book investigates how armed conflicts, geopolitical rivalries, economic sanctions, pandemic-related disruptions, and climate risks exacerbate poverty, inequality, food insecurity, displacement, and institutional fragility. It further examines the implications of these pressures for healthcare systems, energy security, international trade, agricultural production, pharmaceutical supply chains, and economic governance. By encompassing several countries and regions, the work demonstrates how historical inequalities, uneven institutional capacity, and unequal access to resources shape societies' resilience to successive shocks. Particular attention is given to the disproportionate burdens borne by vulnerable populations, including women, children, displaced communities, and economically disadvantaged households. The analysis also challenges conventional assessments of national progress based solely on economic growth, geopolitical influence, or strategic advantage, emphasizing the importance of equitable resource distribution and human welfare. Ultimately, the article demonstrate the book's contribution to understanding global crises as interconnected rather than isolated phenomena. It underscores the importance of integrated policymaking, people-centered diplomacy, sustainable conflict resolution, equitable climate finance, resilient public health systems, and inclusive development. The work offers valuable interdisciplinary insights for researchers, policymakers, development practitioners, and international institutions seeking coordinated, equitable, and sustainable responses to contemporary global challenges.

detail.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is preceded by a preclinical phase of years in which autoantibodies, and in some cohorts markers of intestinal barrier dysfunction, rise before synovitis. Ayurveda describes Amavata, commonly equated with RA, as arising from Ama: incompletely transformed material produced by weak digestive capacity (Agni), carried through the body by Vata and lodged in the joints. Earlier authors have equated Ama with a substancefree radicals, endotoxin, advanced glycation end-products-or linked Agni and Virechana to the gut microbiota in general terms. None of these proposals is tied to a stage of disease or generates a test that could fail. We propose a different, testable claim. The classical definition places Ama at the interface between digestion and the first circulating tissue (rasa). We therefore hypothesise that Ama, as operationalised by validated Ama assessment scales, corresponds to a state-mucosal barrier failure with translocation of luminal products-rather than to any single molecule, and that this state occupies a specific position in the EULAR at-risk continuum: after environmental exposure, before clinically apparent arthritis. Read this way, the Ayurvedic stage model (Ṣaṭkriyākāla) and the biomedical at-risk phases align point for point. The hypothesis yields four predictions. Ama scores should correlate with zonulin-family peptides, LBP, sCD14 and I-FABP independently of CRP; should be higher in ACPA-positive at-risk individuals who progress; should fall with Ama-directed treatment (Langhana, Dīpana-Pācana, Virecana) before disease activity falls; and a composite Ama score should outperform any single barrier marker. Null associations would falsify the gut-barrier reading of Ama. Each prediction can be tested with existing instruments and commercially available assays.

detail.abstract: Repeated security disruptions in the Red Sea between 2023 and 2026 raise questions about whether alternative routes can ensure the fulfillment of contracts involving successive shipments. detail.abstract: Maternal mortality in the United States remains high and displays an upward trend in contrast with the declining OECD average. Hospital closures and obstetric service losses expanded “maternity care deserts” with limited conventional (in-person) care availability, which may exacerbate these figures. Access to conventional care may also be constrained by communicable disease risk (seasonal conditions or pandemics), or by patient specific conditions that limit travel. Increased telehealth availability may improve care, both directly and by compensating for limited conventional care access in the postpartum (after birth) period. Whether telehealth delivers on this potential remains unclear, with little evidence from large-scale observational data on postpartum care. Using health care claims data on 115,644 births associated with 2,215 providers across the US, we investigate care utilization before and after a period of rapid telehealth expansion and reduced conventional care access. We compare postpartum (after birth) care utilization of women giving birth between November 2019 and November 2020, the period subject to the telehealth shock, to a control group of women giving birth in the same months a year earlier. Our results indicate that telehealth partially offset losses in conventional care during a period of reduced conventional channel availability and rapid telehealth expansion. Telehealth may support postpartum care generally, and help maintain care utilization when conventional options are limited. These benefits are especially pronounced for high-risk mothers, offsetting their differential reduction in conventional care. Our findings support policy shifts that encourage reimbursement of telehealth services, especially for high-risk groups where conventional care may be constrained.

detail.abstract: This study addresses the question of whether inclusionary zoning impacts disadvantaged neighborhoods by serving as a signal for an up-and-coming neighborhood, thereby triggering gentrification. We attempt to answer this question by analyzing data from two cities, New York City and Paris, respectively—two superstar cities where gentrification has spread beyond the ripest neighborhoods for development. Overall, although inclusionary zoning does appear to encourage new development, it does not appear to be a Trojan horse that, in the guise of bringing in affordable housing, also serves as a catalyst for rising housing prices and rents, thereby spurring gentrification. We contrast subjects exposed to the policy intervention with subjects that were not, both before and after the policy has been implemented. The assumption underlying our Difference-inDifferences (DiD) approach is that whatever the trend in the relationship in the outcomes of interest between the treatment and control groups, if the policy intervention has no impact on the outcomes of interest, that trend should continue. To the extent the relationship in the trends changes contemporaneously with the policy intervention, we can make credible causal claims about the policy intervention’s impact on the outcomes of interest. In both New York City and Paris, we found evidence that the incentives offered by inclusionary zoning programs impacted new development in both cities, with new development in inclusionary zones outpacing development in the comparison areas. We found no strong evidence in either New York City or Paris that the adoption of inclusionary zoning had led to increases in the price of homes sold in the inclusionary zones themselves. Instead, in Paris, sales prices actually increased more slowly in the inclusionary zones. In New York City, we did not see any strong evidence that rent levels in inclusionary zones had accelerated after the adoption of inclusionary zones. In Paris, there was some evidence that rents rose more quickly in inclusionary zones. A key takeaway from our analyses is that, despite New York and Paris being very different cities, with the former much more market-driven, and the latter more beholden to centralized state planning, their inclusionary zoning programs performed similarly in terms of incentivizing new development. In both cities, policymakers were able to thread the proverbial needle and require developers to provide affordable housing, while refraining from being so onerous as to discourage any development at all. The impact on housing costs were mixed, with New York witnessing no discernible change in housing costs in inclusionary zones, while Paris saw declines in sales prices but increases in rents. Our results, which will be strengthened by further research, show that inclusionary zoning—even when implemented in more disadvantaged neighborhoods—can be evaluated on its own merits as a tool that can produce affordable housing, without necessarily serving as a catalyst for gentrification.

detail.abstract:
Background: The globalization of Ayurveda is accompanied by its growing integration into health systems, endorsed by the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Strategy 2025-2034, and by rising demands for evidence of safety and effectiveness. This raises a question that is rarely asked directly: what happens to a traditional medical practice when it becomes an object of scientific validation? 

Methods: This conceptual analysis uses Panchakarma, the purificatory therapeutics of Ayurveda, as a case. It draws on the anthropology of Asian medicines and science and technology studies, WHO policy documents, methodological literature on complex interventions, and published clinical research on Ayurveda read for its design decisions. The author's own clinical trial in Amāvāta (rheumatoid arthritis) serves as a reflexive case, supplemented by anonymized field material from three years of clinical work in a Panchakarma department. 

Results: Globalization transforms Panchakarma through a sequence of expanding use, institutional integration, demand for evidence, and translation into biomedical categories. Translation occurs at three sites where context can be lost: the operationalization of concepts such as āma, the standardization of an individualized therapeutic sequence, and the selection of outcomes. At each site, data legible to biomedicine are produced at the cost of substituting a new object for the one the tradition describes. 

Conclusion: The conventional trial model answers a narrower question than the one asked of it. Existing methodological resources, including whole-systems research, model validity, the Medical Research Council framework for complex interventions, and pragmatic, individualized trial designs, allow traditional practices to be evaluated in their own structure and against their own criteria without lowering requirements of safety, quality and effectiveness.

detail.abstract: Recent decades have seen a strong commitment in development theory and practice towards the idea of promoting homeownership among low-income families, partly based on the idea that property formalization constitutes an important vehicle for social mobility and economic development. However, the empirical evidence on this theory is not conclusive. This paper aims to explore this idea using evidence from Chile, a country that has shown high success in moving low-income families from the informal to the formal housing sector. The data for the analysis comes from a comprehensive survey conducted in 2008 with a representative sample of two groups of low-income households in Santiago: the first group living in an irregular settlement, the second living in subsidized formal housing. Through the use of statistical methods that allow comparison of these samples (matching strategies), we find that market behavior among both groups are not considerably different. The analysis shows that there are no statistically significant differences between the two groups with respect to savings and investments in their homes. The only relevant difference we find is that individuals living in formal housing have more access to loans from commercial stores relative to informal dwellers. We argue that the type of geographical relocation to formal housing may affect the market behavior of low-income owners more than tenure security, in a direction that does not necessary benefit their socioeconomic situation.

detail.abstract: We measure the intrinsic complexity of accounting data as its resistance to compression, that is, how much reconstruction loss remains when accounting items are compressed to fewer values. Repeating this for each possible number of compressed values yields a compression-loss curve. A set of ex ante specified validity axioms implies a unique scalar measure of intrinsic complexity, which is the average of this curve. Applying it to 30 Compustat items from 1963 to 2024, we show that intrinsic complexity has risen about sixfold over that period. Most of the rise occurs within industries, and it comes both from firms entering the sample and from firms already in it in 1963. From 1995 to 2024, intrinsic complexity also rises in every major world region, not only the US. An analysis of major US standards and IFRS adoptions does not support accounting standards as the main driver of the rise we document. Firm-years whose accounts are harder to compress also have larger analyst forecast errors and more dispersed forecasts.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping the American energy landscape. Data centers demand vast amounts of reliable power, and small modular reactors have emerged as a leading solution. Tribal nations, whose land the federal government holds in trust, are uniquely positioned to host this development. Yet the Atomic Energy Act extends its cooperative federal-state framework to states, territories, and the District of Columbia, but not to tribes. As a result, tribal nuclear projects face uncertain state authority, case-by-case preemption analysis, and discretionary federal lease approvals that deter investment.

This Comment argues that Congress should amend the Atomic Energy Act to treat federally recognized tribes as states, modeled on the Clean Air Act. Although existing statutory and case law suggests a pathway for tribal nuclear development, that pathway remains too uncertain to support billion-dollar investments. The proposed amendment would leave radiological safety to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission while recognizing tribal authority over the economic and land-use decisions reserved to states. In doing so, it would transform the federal trust relationship from paternalistic gatekeeping into a partnership that honors each tribe’s sovereign right to decide.

detail.abstract: Using 502 regular-review changes to the Nifty 50 and Nifty Next 50 from 2005 to 2026, built from primary NSE notices and exchange price files, I study how forced index trading moves prices in India. Since 2020, deleted stocks have outperformed added stocks by 1.9 percentage points in the session after the index changes (t = 5.9), with a positive spread on 12 of 14 rebalance dates. The pattern is absent before 2020 and survives placebo tests on ordinary days and random stocks. Announcement effects are clear over the full sample (3.4% for the Nifty 50, t = 5.2). The changes are partly predictable from the published rules, yet no average drift is detectable between the data cutoff and the notice, and announcement returns are similar for changes the rule predicted and those it missed. Comparing full execution at the benchmark close with the next close gives a modeled timing cost to index funds of roughly ₹8.8bn (~US$94mn) between 2021 and 2026. Returns from buying after announcements are statistically inconclusive; taking the other side at the close captured the reversal in a closing-price backtest, before execution frictions.

detail.abstract: Plug-in balcony photovoltaics are a new residential solar technology accessible to both renters and owner-occupiers, with more than 1.2 million systems already installed in Germany. We develop a closed-form capital budgeting framework for these systems. Under zero export remuneration and a flat retail tariff, the average self-consumption ratio, the share of generation consumed on site, is a sufficient statistic for net present value. Without storage, the break-even self-consumption ratio is 10.5 percent, well below the rates estimated for German households. Internal rates of return range from 15 to 37 percent across household types, with payback periods of 2.7 to 6.2 years. A 2 kW p system with a 2 kWh battery requires a higher upfront outlay but shifts midday generation into the evening, and returns 18 to 23 percent. The investment is also profitable in Austria, and marginally so in France. Because the system is portable, it earns a positive return for most tenants with short tenancies as well. When all valuation inputs are varied jointly, the investment remains profitable in the large majority of cases. Where it does not, the outcome is driven primarily by the household's discount rate.

detail.abstract: This paper empirically examines how information-sharing platform design shapes consumer search under government-mandated price disclosure. In our retail gasoline market setting, after the government introduces mandatory real-time, station-level price disclosure, consumers initially access prices through a government-run website that requires manual location searches. One year later, the government launches an app with geolocation and automatic notifications, encouraging consumers to search when nearby station prices begin to fall. In this way, the app reduces the cost of obtaining locally relevant, timely price information for fuel purchasing decisions. The sequential website-app rollout thus offers a unique opportunity to examine how platform design shapes search behavior and competitive outcomes. Using real-time search and pricing data from the government's website and app, we find that the app increases long-run search intensity more than sixfold. We then provide novel direct evidence of asymmetric search behavior, finding search is 150% higher in response to a 1-cent-per-liter price increase than a 1-cent-per-liter decrease and remains substantially higher in the weeks thereafter. Platform design also matters for search asymmetry, as the app induces much stronger search behavior in response to negative cost shocks than would otherwise occur. Lastly, the app launch is associated with a 2.4 centper-liter (1.8%) reduction in prices relative to neighboring retail gasoline markets without mandatory price disclosure, underscoring how platform design shapes the intensity and direction of consumer search and competitive effects.

detail.abstract: We study how schools seeking to maximize human capital investment should group students taking a common standardized test. detail.abstract: Unemployment remains a persistent socioeconomic challenge with profound impacts on individuals and economies. detail.abstract: In April 2025, the European Commission fined Apple EUR 500 million for breaching Article 5(4) of the Digital Markets Act (DMA). The Commission found that Apple's 17% commission on purchases made within seven days of a link-out was incompatible with the requirement that steering be "free of charge". Apple first replaced that fee with interim terms in June 2025. Since 1 October 2026, it has charged a 15% "Store Services Commission" on purchases initiated within seven days of a link tap or scan. The new fee keeps the seven-day attribution mechanism of the condemned fee. Like that fee, it recurs on later automatic renewals of subscriptions. A Commission spokesperson has nonetheless welcomed the new terms and was reported as saying that the Commission was not, at this stage, considering periodic penalty payments. More than 30 months after Article 5(4) started to apply, it is time for the Commission either to enforce its Decision or to explain clearly why it will not. This paper makes three points. First, measured against the Commission's own decision, the new fee does not comply with Article 5(4). Second, the Commission's public welcome of terms that reproduce the key features of the condemned fee creates legal uncertainty for developers and weakens the credibility of DMA enforcement. Third, the DMA offers a route that does not require the Commission to set a price: the non-discrimination limb of Article 6(12), a provision that the Commission is bound to enforce. Apple charges a sales commission to apps that sell digital goods and services, but none to apps that sell physical goods and services, although both use the same core App Store services. That difference in treatment is hard to justify. Unlike Article 5(4), this route could examine not only the fee on steered sales but also the commissions Apple charges on In-App Purchase and on alternative payment solutions within the app. The paper closes with the options open to the Commission and to business users.

detail.abstract: This study uses 4,780 individual wage records from Belper Mill, a cotton firm during the British Industrial Revolution, to examine how wage levels, wage structures, and inequality differed across three technology stages: a Water-frame stage, a Mule-led mixed spinning stage, and a Large power-assisted mule stage. detail.abstract: Social media platforms punish accounts, but their automated enforcement systems judge content. Ordinarily the two line up, because the person who controls an account is the person who posts from it. Account takeover breaks that link. This paper uses a documented case, the author's own, in which Facebook's security systems detected a hijacking while it was under way: they recorded the hijacker's session in Vietnam, Arizona and New Jersey within half an hour, emailed the owner that someone may have accessed the account without permission, and undid the hijacker's attempt to rename the account "Meta Verified." A few hours later a separate enforcement system permanently disabled the account for content the hijacker had posted, and the appeal was denied. Evidence from state attorneys general, victim surveys, news reports, litigation and Meta's own Oversight Board suggests the case is not unusual. The failure is one of attribution rather than classification: a system can judge a post correctly and still punish the wrong person. A simple economic account explains why the error persists. The platform bears little of the cost of a false positive, the sanction deters no one, and lock-in and automated appeals blunt both exit and voice. The same account points to inexpensive remedies, chief among them a rule that no account-level sanction be imposed without first consulting the platform's own compromise signals.

detail.abstract: This paper surveys long-term projections of global GDP per capita and presents the authors' own projections through 2050 using a multicountry-multisector general equilibrium model (G-Cubed). Studies generally agree that global GDP per capita growth will continue to slow in the coming decades, driven by several global challenges such as rapid population aging, slower technological progress (in pre-AI projections), weaker capital investment, and stagnating educational attainment. Projections tend to be consistent for advanced economies but vary considerably for developing regions, highlighting the importance of alternative methodologies and assumptions, as well as inherent long-term uncertainty. While existing studies rely on neoclassical models with an aggregate production sector, the G-Cubed model takes a disaggregated approach to projecting productivity and output that accounts for dynamic interactions between sectors and across economies. The authors' projections incorporate the impacts of three fundamental factors: productivity growth, population aging, and climate change. Productivity growth in advanced economies is expected to slow, but AI could counteract the decline and serve as an engine for sustained growth. Population aging in most advanced economies will continue to constrain labor supply, potentially reducing GDP per capita through changes in age structure. Climate change poses challenges to economic growth through multiple channels, with moderate quantitative impacts by midcentury. The extent to which developing regions can boost productivity, leverage demographic advantages, and navigate climate change will depend on policy choices as well as governance and institutional improvements. Finally, the paper discusses the implications of geopolitical fragmentation, government debt, and public infrastructure on economic growth.

detail.abstract: Sovereign bond yields in emerging economies differ from those in advanced economies due to default risk and the composition of currency and ownership of government debt. As a result, fiscal consolidation can transmit through multiple channels, the relative importance of which is not clear ex-ante. We address this by decomposing 10-year sovereign yields in 17 emerging markets into default risk premia, expected short rates, and term premia. We show that vulnerabilities in debt composition—high foreign currency borrowing (original sin), large foreign holdings of local currency debt (original sin redux), and large domestic holdings of foreign currency debt—are associated with both higher default risk and term premia. We find that projected fiscal improvements do not translate to changes in the default risk premia in these economies. Instead, in more vulnerable countries, the adjustment operates mainly through the term premia. A 1 percentage point improvement in the 5-year-ahead primary balance lowers the 5-year, 5-year-ahead forward rate by about 20 basis points over 3 years. These results suggest that debt composition, rather than the fiscal stance alone, governs the transmission of fiscal consolidation to sovereign yields in emerging economies.

detail.abstract: Background. National income is the strongest single predictor of how much a country spends on health. Comparing actual with income-predicted spending shows whether a country mobilises more or less for health than its economic capacity implies. Rwanda is frequently cited as a country that achieves more than its income would suggest, but its position on the regional spending-income curve, and how that position has changed during two decades of rapid economic growth, has not been quantified. Methods. We analysed WHO Global Health Expenditure Database data (December 2025 release) for the 47 WHO African Region member states, 2003-2023 (966 country-years). Current health expenditure (CHE) per capita and its components were regressed on GDP per capita, both in purchasing power parity (PPP) dollars and in logarithms. Between-country elasticities used year fixed effects; within-country elasticities added country fixed effects, with standard errors clustered by country. For each year we estimated Rwanda's expected spending from a regression fitted to all other African Region countries and reported the ratio of actual to expected spending, its 95% prediction interval and Rwanda's percentile among regional residuals. The same procedure was applied to domestic government, external and out-of-pocket (OOP) spending, and to six East African comparators. Six sensitivity analyses varied the currency, functional form and comparison sample. Results. Health spending rose with income at a between-country elasticity of 0.89 (95% CI 0.78-1.01) and a within-country elasticity of 0.77 (0.66-0.88). Government health spending was income-elastic between countries (1.27; 1.06-1.47); external funding showed no association with income (-0.15;-0.57 to 0.28). From 2003 to 2012 Rwanda spent 46-68% more than its income predicted, placing it between the 84th and 91st percentiles of the region. The ratio fell to 0.96-1.14 from 2017 onwards and stood at 0.98 in 2023 (CHE per capita PPP$177 against PPP$181 expected; 54th percentile). Over the same period Rwanda's GDP per capita rose 4.5-fold and its CHE per capita 3.3-fold. In 2023 Rwanda's domestic government spending was 1.95 times the expected level (89th percentile), external funding 1.65 times, and OOP spending 0.13 times, the lowest in the region. Results were stable across all sensitivity analyses (2023 ratio 0.94-1.08). Conclusions. Rwanda moved from a high outlier to the regional norm on total health spending as its economy grew faster than its health budget. Its distinctive feature in 2023 lies in composition: government spending close to twice the expected level and household OOP payments far below it. Sustaining financial protection as external funding declines will require public health spending to keep pace with economic growth.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the modern residential estate as a contemporary iteration of Garrett Hardin’s "Tragedy of the Commons," where individual self-interest and structural governance failures threaten shared community resources. Focusing on the intersection of private property and collective responsibility, the study contrasts the mature, litigious Common Interest Development (CID) and Homeowners Association (HOA) framework of suburban Maryland in the United States with the rapidly formalizing, custom-rooted gated developments of urban Accra, Ghana.

The analysis unpacks the "middleman trap," wherein profit-driven management companies and absentee developers exploit shared amenities or defer maintenance, leaving residents trapped between analog friction and corporate control. While suburban Maryland relies on statutory automation, assessment liens, and foreclosure, Accra’s evolving landscape navigates a complex hybrid of customary land tenure, leaseholds, and progressive statutory anchors—specifically the Land Act 2020 (Act 1036) and the Real Estate Agency Act 2020 (Act 1047) enforced by the Real Estate Agency Council (REAC).

Synthesizing Elinor Ostrom’s principles of common-pool resource governance with emerging Property Technology (PropTech), mobile money integrations, and grassroots corporate structures (such as Companies Limited by Guarantee), the paper demonstrates how communities can transition from adversarial rule enforcement to participatory relationship stewardship. Ultimately, the study reframes residential estates as vital nodes of local civic infrastructure—micro-democracies capable of converting governance from a conflict generator into a sustainable, cooperative civic ecosystem.

detail.abstract: We study price competition between two differentiated retailers that receive a reputational reward for being named cheapest in third-party comparisons. A retailer can increase its probability of winning the comparison by cutting its price, but will then earn less in the regular retail market. When comparisons are perfectly accurate and the gap in retailers' marginal costs is sufficiently small relatively to the reward, retailers randomize their prices: a predictable price would invite the rival to undercut it slightly and win the comparison. The comparison induces the retailers to reduce their expected prices by the same amount even if their marginal costs differ. The price reduction is smaller the larger the cost difference, and it is zero if the difference is sufficiently large. Comparisons then merely transfer reputational rents to the more efficient retailer. Imprecise comparisons can induce retailers to set predictable and lower prices than if the comparison is accurate. detail.abstract: AI is widely predicted to commoditize expert advice and displace the human experts who provide it. In a model of financial advice, we show when and how AI can instead expand the expert sector. Households delegate wealth to an adviser whose advice they must take partly on trust. As an auditor, AI is a complement to advisers that makes their advice less risky to act on; as an outside option, it is a substitute that improves how households invest on their own. We support these channels with data from the U.S. financial advisory industry, measuring how far AI can audit or replace disputed advice and how advisers themselves use AI. Calibrated to the industry in 2021, the model implies that when AI raises households' own expected returns by one percentage point, advised assets rise by about 70 percent. Fees also rise, so advisers capture the gains from auditing and cheaper production of quality, especially those serving wealthier households.

detail.abstract: How do citizens evaluate the legitimacy of automated decision-making (ADM) in public administration? Existing research highlights the importance of procedural fairness, performance, and institutional design, often assuming that citizens assess these features in a neutral and consistent way. Drawing on theories of motivated reasoning from political psychology and behavioral public administration, we challenge this assumption by arguing that outcome favorability systematically shapes how citizens attend to and evaluate procedural information when evaluating the legitimacy of ADM systems. We test this argument using a preregistered survey experiment conducted in Finland (N = 2,040) that combines an outcome-based vignette with a conjoint experiment manipulating key procedural features of an ADM system, including human oversight, accountability, cost, and data practices, in the context of electronic travel authorization. We show that citizens' evaluations of these procedural features depend systematically on whether the ADM system produces politically preferred outcomes. We theorize and empirically assess two mechanisms underlying this pattern: selective attention to procedural information and biased evaluation of procedural safeguards. Evidence from both the conjoint estimates and open-ended survey responses indicates that outcome favorability activates motivated reasoning, shaping which procedural features citizens attend to and how they weight them. The observed effects are concentrated among ideologically committed respondents, even in the lowpolarization context of Finland. Rather than treating biased responses to ADM as isolated cognitive errors, we conceptualize them as part of a broader motivated reasoning process that conditions legitimacy judgments of administrative authority. The study integrates institutional and cognitive perspectives on legitimacy and highlights why procedural improvements alone may be insufficient to secure public acceptance of ADM in public administration.

detail.abstract: As content-commerce platforms increasingly integrate user-generated content with product transactions, AI summaries are becoming an important user-facing information tool for organizing and presenting productrelated information. By providing consumers with summarized product information before they access creator-generated content, AI summaries may improve purchase conversion while redirecting consumer traffic and reshaping creators' content-quality incentives. Despite their growing adoption, the economic implications of AI summaries for platforms and creators remain underexplored. To address this gap, we develop a game-theoretic model in which a content-commerce platform chooses AI-summary informativeness and competing creators choose content quality. Our analysis shows that the platform introduces AI summaries when advertising revenue per unit of regular-content traffic is sufficiently low. We further identify several counterintuitive findings. First, introducing AI summaries improves creators' content quality but may leave them worse off when increased quality-investment costs outweigh additional commission revenue. Second, a greater platform weight on content quality can reduce both optimal AI-summary informativeness and creators' equilibrium content quality. Third, a higher commission rate may induce the platform to provide less informative AI summaries, despite increasing its revenue per transaction. Finally, a higher product price can increase optimal AI-summary informativeness while reducing creators' equilibrium content quality. These findings provide managerial insights for platforms in designing AI summaries and for creators in making content-quality investment decisions.

Enterprise AI programs often spend months in pilots without establishing how a deployment will change operating costs or service outcomes. This paper proposes a four-part delivery sequence: select work with measurable value, establish controls before production, build adoption into everyday workflows, and adjust based on observed performance.

ServiceNow provides the technical reference point, with particular attention to the CMDB, Common Service Data Model (CSDM), workflow integrations, and AI-enabled service operations.

A twelve-month simulation of eight hypothetical use cases compares a value-ranked implementation sequence with a seeded random order and different assumptions about governance and adoption. These figures are scenario outputs, not customer savings or forecasts. The practical contribution is a set of deployment decisions, measurement definitions, and reproducible assumptions that enterprises can adapt to their own workloads.

detail.abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) technologies allow medical devices, wearable sensors and clinical software to detect patient deterioration and escalate emergency alerts without bedside presence. The value of these systems, however, depends on the reliable and secure delivery of alerts and on the way healthcare personnel respond to them. This paper presents a conceptual synthesis of the architecture and operation of IoT-based healthcare emergency response systems, using recent work on emergency alert reliability as its central source. It analyses latency, packet loss, message delivery failure, network disruption and recovery strategies; evaluates cybersecurity threats, including those enabled by generative artificial intelligence; and examines how human behaviour, leadership and safety culture influence emergency communication and patient safety. It also considers machine learning and decision support, patient privacy, data integrity, interoperability, scalability and ethical deployment. Evidence from other sectors, including vehicle-to-everything networks, oil and gas operations and school counselling, is used analogically and is identified as such. The paper proposes an integrated framework linking IoT architecture, communication reliability, cybersecurity, human response and patient safety, and states five testable hypotheses. No new empirical data are reported, and the framework is a proposal for future evaluation rather than an established finding.

detail.abstract: The International Telecommunication Union's Radiocommunication Sector (ITU-R) finalized Recommendation ITU-R M.2160-0 in November 2023, formally establishing the IMT (International Mobile Telecommunications)-2030 framework that will govern sixth-generation (6G) mobile systems in the way Recommendation M.2083-0 governed IMT-2020 (5G). This paper uses that standardization milestone as its starting point rather than its conclusion, and asks a narrower, more practical question than most 6G surveys: given the concrete, quantitative targets ITU-R has now set, what layered network architecture and technology roadmap would let the Internet of Things (IoT) actually absorb those gains, and on what timeline. We propose a three-plane reference architecture, separating connectivity, network intelligence, and service delivery, and use it to organize a technical review of the physical-layer, network-intelligence, and non-terrestrial enablers that must mature together for 6G-IoT to be deployable rather than merely specified. Particular attention is given to two threads that receive comparatively little treatment in adjacent literature: the integration of non-terrestrial platforms (low-Earth-orbit satellites, high-altitude platform stations, and uncrewed aerial vehicles) as a first-class connectivity layer for IoT devices in terrain that terrestrial radio access networks cannot economically reach, and the standardization and security transition-including post-quantum cryptographic migration-that must be substantially complete before large-scale commercial deployment can begin near the end of this decade. We compile ITU-R's quantitative IMT-2020-to-IMT-2030 target trajectory, map six representative IoT application domains against their latency, throughput, reliability, density, and coverage requirements, and set out an indicative standardization timeline running from the 2023 framework recommendation through anticipated initial commercial deployment around 2030. The paper closes by identifying the technical and non-technical obstacles most likely to determine whether that timeline holds.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has moved from systems that answer to systems that act. Agents built on large language models (LLMs) now plan, call tools, keep memory and hand work to other agents. Explainable AI (XAI) was built for a different object: one model, one input and one output. This paper argues that the gap between what agentic systems do and what anyone can explain about them behaves like a debt. Each unexplained decision is a small loan taken against future understanding. The loan carries interest. It grows when later actions build on earlier unexplained ones. It falls due when a regulator, an auditor or a harmed person asks why. The paper introduces the construct of explainability debt and separates four sources: delegation debt, trajectory debt, faithfulness debt and composition debt. It then proposes the Autonomy-Explanation Ledger, a framework that ties four tiers of agent autonomy to specific explanation obligations. Six propositions describe how the debt accrues and how it can be repaid. An Explainability Debt Index is proposed as a practical measure with five components. The paper closes with design patterns for paying the debt down, an illustration from enterprise finance, and implications for research, practice and policy under the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act. The contribution is conceptual. It reframes explainability for agentic AI as a balance-sheet item to be managed over time, not a feature to be switched on at deployment.

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can perform some legal research, drafting and document-review tasks substantially faster than lawyers working unaided and, in several benchmarks, selected tools have matched or exceeded lawyer baselines on defined tasks. The economic significance of these developments for law firms depends on the time and expertise required to turn such outputs into advice that clients can use. On that basis, this article predicts that the main beneficiaries of these tools are senior lawyers, who know what to ask and can tell good output from bad, while their first casualties are junior lawyers, whose traditional tasks are those that machines perform best. This does not mean that law firms will stop hiring associates, but that they will hire fewer of them, look for different qualities and train them differently. Nor is the threat confined to juniors since, given the pace at which the tools are improving, senior associates and even partners may be exposed tomorrow. The article argues that the claim that the lawyer of the future must become a "legal engineer" rests on a misunderstanding, as firms will need some engineers and data scientists but, above all, lawyers who are AI literate. It also argues that law schools should respond to AI by strengthening analytical reasoning, advocacy, logic and economics rather than by teaching the tools themselves. It then examines the consequences of AI for law firm management, including whether the leverage model on which large firms have built their profitability can survive, and warns clients against "self-medication", which creates risks of poor decisions, liability and loss of legal professional privilege. It ends with the question of which tools firms should adopt. The specialist platforms, such as Harvey and Legora, face uncertain economics and depend on frontier model providers that now compete with them, while niche players offering superior value in narrow areas may prove to be the best complements to frontier models. As no one knows how this market will evolve, firms should avoid dependence on any single supplier.

detail.abstract: Economists have recognized the flaws in GDP for decades. Some have proposed fixes. None have taken. The national accounts for the stock of human time do not seek to bury GDP but to stand side-by-side with it. This paper is a brief summary of national hours accounts which I have proposed, derived, and calibrated in a companion paper. The stock of human time was worth $4.2 quadrillion in 2025. Small innovations result in large values. People alive today would be willing to pay about $9 trillion, in total, to free an hour a week from chores and about $3.9 trillion for an extra month of life expectancy. GDP per capita does not reflect a large portion of well-being coming from non-wage hours. Economists can keep using GDP for what it is worth but need to supplement it, for policymaking and research, with the time accounts described here.

detail.abstract: Can a one-state representation of the forward-rate curve satisfy forecast consistency, arbitragefree pricing, physical stationary equilibrium and long-forward restrictions simultaneously? We give a conditional compatibility classification for an exactly affine instantaneous-forward curve with a positive square-root short-rate diffusion. An interior hump in instantaneous-forward volatility selects a non-restoring affine risk-neutral drift but remains compatible with a broad family of restoring physical stationary laws, including non-CIR dynamics; neither pricing nor stationarity identifies a unique physical density or market price of risk. A distinct and explicitly optional assumption-that the stationary physical expected forward curve is globally nondecreasing-implies that its physical mean short rate does not exceed the invariant mean of the long-forward measure, θ P ≤ θ L. On the humped branch, writing u = θ P /ρ for the ratio to the asymptotic forward rate and R > 1 for the instantaneous-forward volatility hump ratio, the restriction is u ≤ [1-√︁ 1-1/R]/2; equivalently, 0 < u < 1/2 and R ≤ [4u(1-u)]-1. A stationary-density-score interpretation clarifies how physical and pricing compatibility coefficients differ. Limited fitted-Treasury-yield diagnostics do not identify the pricing branch: a flat loading performs almost as well as the Riccati loading, while short-/long-tenor proxies cannot reject the mean inequality. The framework identifies which joint restrictions are demonstrable, which require additional geometry, and which physical features remain unidentified.

detail.abstract:
Introduction A study of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo concluded that human movement, measured with mobile phone data, was the principal driver of early spread between health zones. Mobile phone data show how many people travel between zones, not who carried the infection or how it passed to others. We asked whether these data can show how the virus spread, and not only where it appeared next.

Methods We followed a registered protocol. First, at 16 weekly dates (July to October 2026), we ranked health zones by their risk of reporting a first case, using only data available on each date, with and without mobile phone data. Second, we simulated epidemics on the real map, population and travel of 106 health zones. Six scenarios differed only in how infection crossed between zones; all matched the observed outbreak (200 epidemics each).

Results The model using mobile phone data placed 48% of zones reporting a first case within 14 days among its 20 highest-risk zones, against 34% for a road-distance model (difference 14 percentage points; 95% interval 5 to 28). In the top 10, both placed 22%. At most 7.5% of top-20 zones reported a case. In simulations, the mobile phone model performed the same when infected travellers spread the virus and when travel spread nothing (45.9% vs 46.2% of new zones in the top 10). With data up to 1 June, a model of travel links between zones detected these links in at most 1 of 200 epidemics, even when they were real. When only case detection varied with distance to a laboratory, mobile phone data still showed a significant effect in 79–88% of epidemics.

Conclusions Mobile phone data help to rank zones at risk. They cannot show how Bundibugyo virus spread between zones.
